title.raw: 卷107上 律曆志三上 Volume 107a Treatise 3: Treatise on Music and Calendars 1

sentences.zh: 大聖通天地之至理，極生民之能事，體妙繫於神機，作範留於器象。

translations.literal: The great sage comprehends the supreme principle of Heaven and Earth, exhausts what the living people can accomplish, binds subtle essence to the divine mechanism, and leaves models in vessels and images.
translations.idiomatic: The great sage grasps Heaven and Earth's deepest principles, brings human endeavor to its fullest extent, ties the subtle to divine design, and fixes enduring models in concrete forms and instruments.

sentences.zh: 然則制物成法，故冥賾可尋；

translations.literal: Thus by shaping things and establishing standards, hidden profundities may be traced;
translations.idiomatic: By fashioning things and setting norms, even hidden depths become traceable;

sentences.zh: 推變有因，而化生以驗。

translations.literal: when transformation is pursued there are causes, and generation and transformation are verified thereby.
translations.idiomatic: and when change is pursued systematically, causes emerge and the processes of generation and transformation can be confirmed.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝採竹昆崘之陰，聽鳳岐陽之下，斷自然之物，寫自然之音。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor gathered bamboo on the northern slope of Kunlun, listened to the phoenix below Qiyang, cut what nature provided, and captured nature's tones.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor took bamboo from Kunlun's northern slopes, listened to the phoenix at Qiyang, cut what nature offered, and reproduced nature's own tones.

sentences.zh: 音既協矣，黃鍾以立；

translations.literal: When the tones were harmonized, the Yellow Bell was established;
translations.idiomatic: Once the pitches were in harmony, the Yellow Bell was fixed as the standard;

sentences.zh: 數既生矣，氣亦徵之。

translations.literal: when numbers had been generated, the qi also responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: and once numbers arose from this, vital energy likewise registered their effect.

sentences.zh: 於是乎備數、和聲、審度、嘉量、權衡之用，皆出於茲矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the uses of complete numbers, harmonized sounds, examined measures, excellent capacity, and weights and balances all issued from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this came complete numeration, harmonized music, calibrated length, standard capacity, and weights and balances in full.

sentences.zh: 三古所共行，百王不能易。

translations.literal: What the three antiquities practiced in common, a hundred kings could not alter.
translations.idiomatic: Shared across the three antiquities, no king in a hundred reigns could overturn it.

sentences.zh: 漢孝武置協律之官，元帝時京房明六十律，事為密矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han established the office of pitch harmonization; in Emperor Yuandi's time Jing Fang clarified the sixty pitches—the matter became intricate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Wu created the office of pitch harmonization; under Emperor Yuan, Jing Fang elaborated the sixty-pitch system, and the subject grew exceedingly refined.

sentences.zh: 王莽世，徵天下通鍾律之士，劉歆總而條奏之，最為該博，故班固取以為志。

translations.literal: In Wang Mang's age, masters versed in bells and pitch standards were summoned from throughout the realm; Liu Xin compiled and presented them in orderly memorial—the most comprehensive account—so Ban Gu took it for his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang, experts in bells and pitch were summoned empire-wide; Liu Xin summarized their work in a memorial of unmatched breadth, which Ban Gu adopted for his treatise.

sentences.zh: 後漢待詔嚴嵩頗為知律，至其子宣不傳，遂罷。

translations.literal: In Later Han the expectant official Yan Song was rather knowledgeable in pitch standards, but when his son Xuan did not transmit the art, it came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's expectant official Yan Song knew pitch theory well, but his son Xuan failed to pass it on, and the tradition lapsed.

sentences.zh: 魏世杜夔亦以通樂制律，晉中書監荀勗持夔律校練八音，以謂後漢至魏尺長古尺四分有餘。

translations.literal: In Wei times Du Kui also mastered music and fashioned pitch standards; Jin's Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu took Kui's standards to tune and train the eight sounds, judging that from Later Han to Wei the foot exceeded the ancient foot by more than four tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Du Kui mastered music and set pitch standards; Jin's Xun Xu used Du Kui's pipes to tune the eight sounds and concluded that from Later Han through Wei the standard foot ran more than four tenths longer than the ancient foot.

sentences.zh: 又得古玉律，勗以新律命之，謂其應合，遂改晉調，而散騎侍郎阮咸譏其聲高。

translations.literal: He also obtained ancient jade pitch pipes; Xu named them by the new standards, claimed they matched, and thus altered Jin's tuning—while Palace Attendant Ruan Xian mocked that the pitch was too high.
translations.idiomatic: He also acquired ancient jade pitch pipes, renamed them according to his new standards, declared them a match, and changed Jin's tuning—though Palace Attendant Ruan Xian criticized the pitch as too high.

sentences.zh: 永嘉以後，中原喪亂，考正鍾律，所未聞焉。

translations.literal: After the Yongjia era, the Central Plains fell into chaos, and rectifying bells and pitch standards was unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia, with the heartland in turmoil, no one spoke of correcting bells and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 其存於夷裔，聲器而已。

translations.literal: What survived among the barbarian borderlands was merely musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: All that endured among frontier peoples were the physical instruments themselves.

sentences.zh: 魏氏平諸僭偽，頗獲古樂。

translations.literal: When the Wei house pacified the various usurpers, they obtained a fair measure of ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei conquered the rival states, they recovered a considerable store of ancient music.

sentences.zh: 高祖慮其永爽，太和中詔中書監高閭修正音律，久未能定。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu feared it would be lost forever; in the Taihe era he ordered Director of the Secretariat Gao Lü to correct pitch and music, but for long they could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu feared permanent loss of the tradition; in Taihe he ordered Gao Lü to restore pitch and music, yet years passed without resolution.

sentences.zh: 閭出為相州刺史，十八年，閭表曰：「書稱『同律度量衡』，論云『謹權量，審法度』。

translations.literal: Lü was sent out as governor of Xiangzhou; in the eighteenth year Lü memorialized: "The Documents say 'unify pitch, measure, capacity, and balance'; the Analects say 'be scrupulous with weights and measures, examine standards and models.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü became governor of Xiangzhou, in year eighteen he submitted: "The Documents demand unified pitch, length, capacity, and balance; the Analects require scrupulous weights and careful standards."

sentences.zh: 此四者乃是王者之要務，生民之所由。

translations.literal: These four are the sovereign's essential tasks and the foundation on which the people depend.
translations.idiomatic: These four are essential duties of kingship and the basis on which the people rely.

sentences.zh: 四者何先？

translations.literal: Which of the four comes first?
translations.idiomatic: Which of the four should come first?

sentences.zh: 以律為首。

translations.literal: Pitch standards come first.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch standards come first.

sentences.zh: 豈不以取法之始，求天地之氣故也。

translations.literal: Is it not because at the beginning of taking one's model one seeks the qi of Heaven and Earth?
translations.idiomatic: Surely because at the very start of establishing norms one must seek the vital breath of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『移風易俗，莫尚於樂。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'To transform customs and change habits, nothing surpasses music.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'To transform customs and change habits, nothing surpasses music.

sentences.zh: 』然則樂之所感，其致遠矣。

translations.literal: ' Thus what music stirs reaches far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus the influence of music extends very far indeed.

sentences.zh: 今調音制樂，非律無以克和，然則律者樂之本也。

translations.literal: Now to tune sounds and regulate music, without pitch standards harmony cannot be achieved; thus pitch standards are the root of music.
translations.idiomatic: To tune sounds and compose music today, harmony cannot be achieved without pitch standards; pitch standards are therefore the foundation of music.

sentences.zh: 臣前被敕理樂，與皇宗博士孫惠蔚、太樂祭酒公孫崇等考周官、國語及後漢律曆志，案京房法作準以定律，吹律以調絲，案律寸以孔竹，八音之別，事以粗舉。

translations.literal: Your servant was previously ordered to oversee music; with Imperial Clan academician Sun Huiwei, Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong, and others I examined the Offices of Zhou, the Discourses of the States, and the Later Han Treatise on Pitch and Calendars; following Jing Fang's method I made a pitch pipe to establish the standards, blew the pipes to tune the strings, and bored bamboo according to pitch-standard inches—the distinctions among the eight sounds have been outlined in rough.
translations.idiomatic: I was previously ordered to oversee music; with Imperial Clan academician Sun Huiwei, Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong, and others I studied the Offices of Zhou, the Discourses of the States, and the Later Han treatise on pitch and calendars. Following Jing Fang's method I constructed a pitch pipe to set the standards, used blown pipes to tune the strings, and bored bamboo to pitch-standard dimensions—the eight categories of sound have been sketched in outline.

sentences.zh: 書既三奏，備在前文。

translations.literal: The memorial having been presented three times, the full text is in the preceding passage.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was presented three times; the full account appears in the preceding text.

sentences.zh: 臣年垂七十，日就衰頹，恐一朝先犬馬，竟無絲髮之益，使律法長絕，遺恨沒世，是以慺慺惓惓，不敢忘怠。

translations.literal: Your servant is nearly seventy, daily declining in vigor; I fear that one morning I may precede my hounds and horses and achieve not the slightest benefit, leaving pitch law forever extinct and regret to my dying day—therefore I am earnest and diligent and dare not forget or slacken.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly seventy and growing weaker by the day; I fear I may die before contributing even the smallest service, leaving pitch law extinct forever and carrying regret to my grave—therefore I press on earnestly and dare not slacken.

sentences.zh: 近在鄴見崇，臣先以其聰敏精勤，有挈瓶之智，雖非經國之才，頗長推考之術，故臣舉以教樂，令依臣先共所論樂事，自作鍾磬志議二卷，器數為備，可謂世不乏賢。

translations.literal: Recently at Ye I saw Chong; your servant had earlier judged him intelligent, diligent, and possessed of the wisdom to carry a pitcher—though not talent for governing the state, he is quite skilled in inferential investigation; therefore I recommended him to teach music and had him follow our earlier discussions of music, composing on his own two fascicles of a Treatise on Bells and Chimes—the instruments and numbers are complete; one may say the age is not lacking in talent.
translations.idiomatic: Recently at Ye I met Chong; I had judged him intelligent, diligent, and capable in small matters—though not a statesman, he excels at systematic inquiry. I recommended him to teach music and had him follow our earlier discussions, producing on his own two fascicles on bells and chimes with instruments and numbers fully specified; the age is not without able men.

sentences.zh: 今崇徒教樂童書學而已，不恭樂事，臣恐音律一曠，精賞實難，習業差怠，轉乖本意。

translations.literal: Now Chong merely teaches music youths book-learning and nothing more, not attending to music affairs; your servant fears that once pitch and music are neglected, true appreciation will be hard indeed, practice will slacken, and the original intent will be further betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chong only teaches music students literacy and nothing more, neglecting music itself; I fear that once pitch and music are abandoned, true mastery will be impossible, training will slacken, and the original purpose will be lost.

sentences.zh: 今請使崇參知律呂鍾磬之事，觸類而長之，成益必深。

translations.literal: I now request that Chong be allowed to participate in matters of pitch pipes, bells, and chimes; by extending his knowledge to related categories, the benefit achieved will surely be profound.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Chong be assigned to pitch pipes, bells, and chimes; extending his work by analogy will yield substantial benefit.

sentences.zh: 求持臣先所奏三表勘後漢律曆志，陛下親覽，以求厥衷，俱然易了。

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty take the three tables your servant previously submitted and compare them with the Later Han Treatise on Pitch and Calendars; if Your Majesty personally peruses them to seek the true meaning, all will be readily understood.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty compare my three previously submitted tables with the Later Han treatise on pitch and calendars; a personal review will make the true meaning clear at once.

sentences.zh: 又著作郎韓顯宗博聞強識，頗有史才，粗解音律，亦求令時往參知。

translations.literal: Moreover, Editorial Director Han Xianzong is broadly learned with a strong memory, has considerable talent for history, and has a rough understanding of pitch and music; I also ask that he be sent from time to time to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial Director Han Xianzong is erudite and retentive, talented in historiography, and has some grasp of pitch and music; I also ask that he be sent periodically to assist.

sentences.zh: 臣雖在外官，竊慕古人舉善之義，愚意所及，不能自己，雖則越分，志在補益，願不以言廢人。

translations.literal: Though your servant holds an outside post, I privately admire the ancients' principle of recommending the worthy; what my foolish mind reaches I cannot restrain; though it oversteps my station, my intent is to be of benefit—I pray Your Majesty will not reject the men on account of the words.
translations.idiomatic: Though I serve outside the capital, I admire the ancients' practice of recommending talent; I cannot restrain what I believe worth saying; though I overstep my rank, my aim is the public good—I pray you will not dismiss these men on account of my words.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，并州獲古銅權，詔付崇以為鍾律之準。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming, Bingzhou obtained an ancient bronze weight; an edict entrusted it to Chong to serve as the standard for bells and pitch.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 4, Bingzhou recovered an ancient bronze weight; an edict assigned it to Chong as the standard for bells and pitch.

sentences.zh: 永平中，崇更造新尺，以一黍之長，累為寸法。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era Chong made a new foot-rule, taking the length of one millet grain and accumulating it to form the inch standard.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping, Chong made a new foot-rule by stacking the length of single millet grains to define the inch.

sentences.zh: 尋太常卿劉芳受詔修樂，以秬黍中者一黍之廣即為一分，而中尉元匡以一黍之廣度黍二縫，以取一分。

translations.literal: Soon after, Director of Ceremonies Liu Fang received an edict to revise music, taking the width of one grain of black millet of medium size as one fen; while Commandant of the Guards Yuan Kuang took the width of one grain to span two gaps between grains and thus obtain one fen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Director of Ceremonies Liu Fang was ordered to revise music, defining one fen as the width of a single medium black millet grain; Commandant of the Guards Yuan Kuang, by contrast, used one grain's width to span two grain-gaps and thus obtain one fen.

sentences.zh: 三家紛競，久不能決。

translations.literal: The three schools disputed heatedly and for long could not reach a decision.
translations.idiomatic: The three schools disputed fiercely, and for years no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，高祖詔，以一黍之廣，用成分體，九十黍之長，以定銅尺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe, Emperor Gaozu decreed: use the width of one millet grain to form the fractional units, and ninety millet grains in length to fix the bronze foot-rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 19, Emperor Gaozu decreed that the width of one millet grain should define the fractional units and ninety millet grains in length should fix the bronze foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 有司奏從前詔，而芳尺同高祖所制，故遂典修金石。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized to follow the earlier decree; Fang's foot-rule matched what Emperor Gaozu had established, and therefore he was put in charge of bells and stones.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported compliance with the earlier decree; Fang's foot-rule matched the emperor's standard, so he was placed in charge of bells and stone chimes.

sentences.zh: 迄武定末，未有諳律者。

translations.literal: Down to the end of Wuding, there was no one versed in pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Through the end of the Wuding era, no one was truly versed in pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 正光曆沿革

translations.literal: Evolution of the Zhengguang Calendar
translations.idiomatic: Evolution of the Zhengguang Calendar

sentences.zh: 曆者數之用，探靈測化，窮微極幽之術也。

translations.literal: The calendar is the application of numbers, a technique for probing the numinous and measuring transformation, exhausting the subtle and reaching the most recondite.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar applies number to probe the numinous and measure change—it is the art of exhausting the subtle and penetrating the deepest mysteries.

sentences.zh: 所以上齊七政，下授萬方。

translations.literal: Therefore above it aligns the seven regulators, below it instructs the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: Above it aligns the seven luminaries; below it instructs the myriad regions.

sentences.zh: 自軒轅以還，迄於三代，推元革統，厥事不一也。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor onward down to the Three Dynasties, in establishing the origin and changing the succession, the matter was not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through the Three Dynasties, each era established its own origin and changed its succession—the practice was never uniform.

sentences.zh: 秦世漢興，曆同顓頊，百有餘年，始行三統。

translations.literal: In Qin times and at Han's rise the calendar followed Zhuanxu; after more than a hundred years the Triple Concordance was first adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin and at Han's founding the calendar followed Zhuanxu; only after more than a century did the Triple Concordance system come into use.

sentences.zh: 後漢孝章世改從四分，光和中易以乾象，魏文時用韓翊所定，至明帝行楊偉景初，終於晉朝，無所改作。

translations.literal: In Later Han under Emperor Xiaozhang the Quarter-Remainder was adopted; in the Guanghe era it was changed to the Supernal Icon; in Wei Wendi's time Han Yi's version was used; under Emperor Ming Yang Wei's Jingchu calendar was adopted, and through the Jin dynasty there was no alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Emperor Zhang adopted the Quarter-Remainder calendar; in Guanghe it was replaced by the Supernal Icon; Wei Emperor Wen used Han Yi's system; Ming Emperor employed Yang Wei's Jingchu calendar, and through Jin no further changes were made.

sentences.zh: 司天測象，今古共情，啟端歸餘，為法不等，協日正時，俱有得失。

translations.literal: Those who oversee Heaven and measure the heavens share the same concern in ancient and modern times; in opening the cycle and returning the remainder the methods are not equal, and in harmonizing the sun and correcting the time each has strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial observers ancient and modern share the same concern; methods for opening cycles and handling remainders differ, and each system for harmonizing the sun and correcting time has its strengths and flaws.

sentences.zh: 太祖天興初，命太史令晁崇修渾儀以觀星象，仍用景初曆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing under the Founding Emperor, the Director of Astronomy Chao Chong was ordered to repair the armillary sphere to observe the starry emblems, still using the Jingchu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianxing, the Founding Emperor ordered Director of Astronomy Chao Chong to repair the armillary sphere for observing the heavens, continuing to use the Jingchu calendar.

sentences.zh: 歲年積久，頗以為疏。

translations.literal: As years accumulated, it was widely regarded as loose.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years it came to be regarded as increasingly inaccurate.

sentences.zh: 世祖平涼土，得趙𣤆所修玄始曆，後謂為密，以代景初。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor pacified the Liang region and obtained the Xuanshi calendar compiled by Zhao Fei; later it was judged precise and replaced the Jingchu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu pacified the Liang region and obtained Zhao Fei's Xuanshi calendar; it was later judged more precise and replaced the Jingchu system.

sentences.zh: 真君中，司徒崔浩為五寅元曆，未及施行，浩誅，遂寢。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era, Minister of Works Cui Hao devised a calendar with the Five Yin as origin; before it could be implemented, Hao was executed and the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenjun, Minister of Works Cui Hao devised a calendar using the Five Yin as origin; before it could be adopted, Hao was executed and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 高祖太和中，詔祕書鍾律郎上谷張明豫為太史令，修綜曆事，未成，明豫物故。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Emperor Gaozu, Zhang Mingyu of Shanggu, Secretary Pitch-Standards Officer, was appointed Director of Astronomy to compile calendar affairs; it was not completed before Mingyu died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe, Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhang Mingyu of Shanggu, a secretary pitch-standards officer, as Director of Astronomy to compile the calendar; the work was unfinished when Mingyu died.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，仍歲南討，而宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: After the move to Luoyang, campaigns to the south continued year after year, and the imperial carriage halted in its evening journey.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, southern campaigns continued year after year, and the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明中，詔太樂令公孫崇、太樂令趙樊生等同共考驗。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era of Emperor Shizong, an edict ordered Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong, Director of Imperial Music Zhao Fansheng, and others jointly to examine and verify.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming, Emperor Shizong ordered Gongsun Chong, Zhao Fansheng, and others jointly to examine and verify the calendar.

sentences.zh: 正始四年冬，崇表曰：「臣頃自太樂，詳理金石，及在祕省，考步三光，稽覽古今，研其得失。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhengshi, Chong memorialized: "Your servant has recently come from the Imperial Music Office, where I examined bells and stones in detail, and in the Secretariat I calculated the steps of the three luminaries, reviewed ancient and modern, and studied their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Zhengshi year 4, Chong submitted: "I have recently left the Imperial Music Office, where I examined bells and stones in detail; in the Secretariat I calculated the motions of the sun, moon, and stars, reviewed ancient and modern systems, and studied their merits and flaws.

sentences.zh: 然四序遷流，五行變易，帝王相踵，必奉初元，改正朔，殊徽號、服色，觀于時變，以應天道。

translations.literal: Yet the four seasons flow in succession, the five phases transform and change; emperors follow one another and must uphold the initial origin, reform the calendar and new moon, and differentiate emblems, titles, and colors—observing the changes of the time to respond to Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons succeed one another and the five phases shift; each new emperor must establish a new origin, reform the calendar and new year, and change emblems, titles, and colors—observing the times to align with Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 故易，湯武革命，治曆明時。

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says that Tang and Wu effected revolution and regulated the calendar to clarify the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Changes says that Tang and Wu effected revolution and regulated the calendar to clarify the seasons.

sentences.zh: 是以三五迭隆，曆數各異。

translations.literal: Hence the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rose in succession, each with a different calendar reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rose in turn, each with a different calendar system.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇魏紹天明命，家有率土，戎軒仍動，未遑曆事，因前魏景初曆，術數差違，不協晷度。

translations.literal: I reflect that Great Wei has received Heaven's bright mandate and possesses all within the four seas; the war chariot moves repeatedly and calendar affairs have not yet been attended to; relying on the former Wei's Jingchu calendar, the calculations diverge and do not accord with gnomon measurements.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei has received Heaven's mandate and rules all within the seas; campaigns continue unceasingly and calendar reform has been deferred; the former Wei's Jingchu calendar has grown inaccurate and no longer matches gnomon observations.

sentences.zh: 世祖應期，輯寧諸夏，乃命故司徒、東郡公崔浩錯綜其數。

translations.literal: Shizu responded to the age, pacified all Xia, and ordered the late Minister of Works, Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao, to weave together the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, responding to his age, pacified the realm and ordered the late Minister of Works, Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao, to rework the calendrical calculations.

sentences.zh: 浩博涉淵通，更修曆術，兼著五行論。

translations.literal: Hao was broadly learned and penetratingly versed; he further revised calendrical methods and also authored a Treatise on the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was erudite and penetrating; he revised the calendrical methods and also wrote a treatise on the five phases.

sentences.zh: 是時故司空、咸陽公高允該覽羣籍，贊明五緯，并述洪範。

translations.literal: At that time the late Minister of Works, Duke of Xianyang Gao Yun, had mastered all the classics, assisted in clarifying the five wefts, and also expounded the Great Plan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the late Minister of Works, Duke of Xianyang Gao Yun, had mastered the classics, assisted in clarifying the five planetary paths, and also expounded the Great Plan.

sentences.zh: 然浩等考察未及周密，高宗踐祚，乃用敦煌趙𣤆甲寅之曆，然其星度，稍為差遠。

translations.literal: Yet Hao and the others had not completed their investigation thoroughly; when Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Zhao Fei of Dunhuang's calendar with jiayin as origin was adopted, yet its stellar degrees were somewhat divergent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao's investigation was incomplete; when Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Zhao Fei of Dunhuang's calendar with the jiayin origin was adopted, but its stellar positions were somewhat off.

sentences.zh: 臣輒鳩集異同，研其損益，更造新曆。

translations.literal: Your servant has gathered divergent views, studied what should be added or subtracted, and fashioned a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: I have gathered divergent views, studied what should be revised, and devised a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 以甲寅為元，考其盈縮，晷象周密，又從約省。

translations.literal: Taking jiayin as the origin, I have examined its excess and deficit; the gnomon observations are thorough, and it is also simplified.
translations.idiomatic: With jiayin as the origin, I have examined its excess and deficit; gnomon observations are thorough, and the system is also simplified.

sentences.zh: 起自景明，因名景明曆。

translations.literal: Beginning from Jingming, it is therefore named the Jingming calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning in the Jingming era, it is therefore named the Jingming calendar.

sentences.zh: 然天道盈虛，豈曰必協，要須參候是非，乃可施用。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's Way has its fullness and emptiness—how can one say it must certainly accord? One must cross-check right and wrong through observation before it can be put into use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's Way has its cycles of fullness and emptiness—how can we assume perfect accord? We must verify it through observation before adopting it.

sentences.zh: 太史令辛寶貴職司玄象，頗閑祕數；

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy Xin Baogui, whose office oversees the dark emblems, is quite versed in secret reckonings;
translations.idiomatic: Director of Astronomy Xin Baogui, whose office oversees the heavens, is well versed in arcane calculations;

sentences.zh: 祕書監鄭道昭才學優贍，識覽該密；

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zheng Daozhao is talented and learned, his knowledge comprehensive and penetrating;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Zheng Daozhao is talented and learned, with comprehensive and penetrating knowledge;

sentences.zh: 長兼國子博士高僧裕乃故司空允之孫，世綜文業；

translations.literal: Senior Concurrent Academician of the Imperial University Gao Sengyu is grandson of the late Minister of Works Yun, his family for generations mastering literary learning;
translations.idiomatic: Senior Concurrent Academician of the Imperial University Gao Sengyu, grandson of the late Minister of Works Gao Yun, comes from a family long devoted to scholarship;

sentences.zh: 尚書祠部郎中宗景博涉經史；

translations.literal: Secretary of the Masters of Writing, Bureau of Sacrifices, Zong Jing is broadly versed in the classics and histories;
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jing of the Sacrifices Bureau in the Masters of Writing is broadly versed in the classics and histories;

sentences.zh: 前兼尚書郎中崔彬微曉法術：請此數人在祕省參候。

translations.literal: former Concurrent Secretary Cui Bin has a slight understanding of computational methods: I request that these several persons participate in observation within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: former Concurrent Secretary Cui Bin has some knowledge of computational methods: I ask that these men assist in verification within the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 而伺察晷度，要在冬夏二至前後各五日，然後乃可取驗。

translations.literal: Observing gnomon measurements depends on the five days before and after each of the winter and summer solstices; only then can verification be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon observation requires the five days before and after each solstice; only then can verification be obtained.

sentences.zh: 臣區區之誠，冀效萬分之一。

translations.literal: Your servant's humble sincerity hopes to achieve one ten-thousandth of success.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble way I hope to contribute even the smallest measure of service.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「測度晷象，考步宜審，可令太常卿芳率太學、四門博士等依所啟者，悉集詳察。」

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Measuring gnomon emblems and calculating steps should be done with care; let Director of Ceremonies Fang lead the Imperial University and Four Gates academicians and others according to what was proposed, all to assemble for detailed examination."
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Gnomon measurement and calendrical calculation require care; let Director of Ceremonies Liu Fang lead Imperial University and Four Gates academicians and others as proposed, all to assemble for detailed review."

sentences.zh: 延昌四年冬，侍中、國子祭酒領著作郎崔光表曰：「易稱『君子以治曆明時』；

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Yanxi, Palace Attendant and Chancellor of the Imperial University, Concurrent Editorial Director Cui Guang memorialized: "The Changes says 'The noble man regulates the calendar to clarify the seasons';
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Yanxi year 4, Palace Attendant Cui Guang, Chancellor of the Imperial University and concurrent Editorial Director, submitted: "The Changes says, 'The noble man regulates the calendar to clarify the seasons';

sentences.zh: 書云『曆象日月星辰』，『廼同律度量衡』；

translations.literal: the Documents say 'the calendar emblems are the sun, moon, stars, and constellations,' and 'thus unify pitch, measure, capacity, and balance';
translations.idiomatic: the Documents say, 'the calendar emblems are the sun, moon, stars, and constellations,' and 'thus unify pitch, length, capacity, and balance';

sentences.zh: 孔子陳後王之法，曰『謹權量，審法度』；

translations.literal: Confucius set forth the methods for later kings, saying 'be scrupulous with weights and measures, examine standards and models';
translations.idiomatic: Confucius set forth methods for later kings, saying, 'be scrupulous with weights and measures, examine standards and models';

sentences.zh: 春秋舉『先王之正時也，履端於始』，又言『天子有日官』。

translations.literal: the Spring and Autumn cites 'the former kings corrected the seasons, taking the beginning as the starting point,' and also says 'the Son of Heaven has officers of the sun.'
translations.idiomatic: the Spring and Autumn cites, 'the former kings corrected the seasons, beginning at the year's start,' and also says, 'the Son of Heaven has officers of the sun.'

sentences.zh: 是以昔在軒轅，容成作曆；

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity under the Yellow Emperor, Rong Cheng made the calendar;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in antiquity under the Yellow Emperor, Rong Cheng devised the calendar;

sentences.zh: 逮乎帝唐，羲和察影。

translations.literal: down to Emperor Tang of Yao, Xi and He observed the shadows.
translations.idiomatic: down to Emperor Yao of Tang, Xi and He observed the shadows.

sentences.zh: 皆所以審農時而重民事也。

translations.literal: All were for examining the agricultural seasons and valuing the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: All were meant to determine the agricultural seasons and honor the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，臣自博士遷著作，忝司載述，時舊鍾律郎張明豫推步曆法，治己丑元，草創未備。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe your servant moved from academician to editorial office, unworthily charged with recording; at that time the former pitch-standards officer Zhang Mingyu was calculating the calendar methods, establishing the jichou origin, but the draft was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 11 I moved from academician to the editorial office, charged with historiography; at that time former pitch-standards officer Zhang Mingyu was calculating the calendar with the jichou origin, but the draft remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 及遷中京，轉為太史令，未幾喪亡，所造致廢。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to the central capital he became Director of Astronomy; before long he died and what he had made fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang he became Director of Astronomy; he soon died and his work was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 臣中修史，景明初奏求奉車都尉、領太史令趙樊生，著作佐郎張洪，給事中、領太樂令公孫崇等造曆，功未及訖，而樊生又喪，洪出除涇州長史，唯崇獨專其任。

translations.literal: While your servant was revising the history, at the beginning of Jingming I memorialized requesting Palace Horse Commandant and Concurrent Director of Astronomy Zhao Fansheng, Editorial Assistant Zhang Hong, Palace Attendant and Concurrent Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong, and others to make the calendar; the work was not finished when Fansheng also died, Hong was sent out as chief secretary of Jingzhou, and only Chong alone bore the task.
translations.idiomatic: While I was revising the history, at the start of Jingming I requested that Palace Horse Commandant Zhao Fansheng, concurrent Director of Astronomy, editorial assistant Zhang Hong, and Gongsun Chong, concurrent Director of Imperial Music, compile the calendar; the work was unfinished when Fansheng died, Hong was posted to Jingzhou, and Chong alone carried on.

sentences.zh: 暨永平初，云已略舉。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Yongping it was said to be roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: By the start of Yongping it was said to be roughly complete.

sentences.zh: 時洪府解停京，又奏令重修前事，更取太史令趙勝、太廟令龐靈扶、明豫子龍祥共集祕書，與崇等詳驗，推建密曆。

translations.literal: At that time Hong's term at the prefectural office ended and he remained in the capital; I again memorialized to have the earlier work revised anew, further taking Director of Astronomy Zhao Sheng, Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Pang Lingfu, and Mingyu's son Longxiang to assemble in the Secretariat with Chong and others for detailed verification, to establish a precise calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong's prefectural term ended and he remained in the capital, I again requested revision of the earlier work, appointing Zhao Sheng as Director of Astronomy, Pang Lingfu as Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Mingyu's son Longxiang to join Chong and others in the Secretariat for detailed verification toward a precise calendar.

sentences.zh: 然天道幽遠，測步理深，候觀遷延，歲月滋久，而崇及勝前後並喪。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's Way is remote and obscure, measurement and calculation are profound in principle, observation was prolonged, months and years grew many, and Chong and Sheng in succession both died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's Way is remote, measurement profound, and observation dragged on for years—meanwhile Chong and Sheng died in succession.

sentences.zh: 洪所造曆為甲午、甲戌二元，又除豫州司馬。

translations.literal: The calendar Hong made used the jiawu and jiaxu origins; he was also appointed military aide of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's calendar used the jiawu and jiaxu origins; he was then appointed military aide of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 靈扶亦除蒲陰令。

translations.literal: Lingfu was also appointed magistrate of Puyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu was also appointed magistrate of Puyin.

sentences.zh: 洪至豫州，續造甲子、己亥二元。

translations.literal: When Hong reached Yuzhou, he continued making calendars with the jiazi and jihai origins.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong reached Yuzhou, he continued work on calendars with the jiazi and jihai origins.

sentences.zh: 唯龍祥在京，獨修前事，以皇魏運水德，為甲子元。

translations.literal: Only Longxiang remained in the capital, alone continuing the earlier work, taking Great Wei's fortune as Water Virtue and making jiazi the origin.
translations.idiomatic: Only Longxiang remained in the capital, continuing the earlier work alone, taking Great Wei's Water Virtue fortune and adopting the jiazi origin.

sentences.zh: 兼校書郎李業興本雖不預，亦和造曆，為戊子元。

translations.literal: Concurrent Proofreader Li Yexing, though not originally involved, also collaborated in making a calendar with the wuzi origin.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent proofreader Li Yexing, though not originally involved, also collaborated on a calendar with the wuzi origin.

sentences.zh: 三家之術並未申用。

translations.literal: The methods of all three schools were not put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: None of the three schools' methods was adopted.

sentences.zh: 故貞靜處士李謐私立曆法，言合紀次，求就其兄瑒追取，與洪等所造，遞相參考，以知精粗。

translations.literal: Therefore the retired gentleman of pure retirement Li Mi privately established calendar methods, saying they accorded with chronological order; he sought to have them retrieved from his elder brother Yang's estate and cross-referenced with what Hong and others had made, to know coarse from fine.
translations.idiomatic: The retired gentleman Li Mi privately devised a calendar, claiming it matched the chronological order; he sought to recover it from his brother Yang's estate and cross-reference it with Hong's and others' work to judge their relative accuracy.

sentences.zh: 臣以仰測晷度，實難審正，又求更取諸能算術兼解經義者前司徒司馬高綽、駙馬都尉盧道虔、前冀州鎮東長史祖瑩、前并州秀才王延業、謁者僕射常景等日集祕書，與史官同檢疏密；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that measuring gnomon degrees by looking upward is truly hard to verify correctly; I further request to take those skilled in calculation who also understand the meaning of the classics—former Secretary of the Masters of Works Gao Chuo, Commandant of Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law Lu Daoqian, former chief secretary of eastern Ji for Jizhou Zu Ying, former provincial graduate of Bingzhou Wang Yanye, and Master of Ceremonies Chang Jing—to assemble daily in the Secretariat with the historiographers jointly to examine what is loose or tight;
translations.idiomatic: I find that gnomon measurement from below is hard to verify with certainty; I further ask that skilled calculators who also understand the classics—former Secretariat Marshal Gao Chuo, Commandant of Horse Lu Daoqian, former eastern Ji chief secretary Zu Ying, former Bingzhou graduate Wang Yanye, and Master of Ceremonies Chang Jing—assemble daily in the Secretariat with the historiographers to examine each system's strengths and weaknesses;

sentences.zh: 并朝貴十五日一臨，推驗得失，擇其善者奏聞施用。

translations.literal: and that court nobles visit once every fifteen days to test strengths and weaknesses, select the best, memorialize, and put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: and that court nobles review the work every fifteen days, test each system's merits, select the best, and memorialize for adoption.

sentences.zh: 限至歲終。

translations.literal: The deadline is the year's end.
translations.idiomatic: The deadline is the end of the year.

sentences.zh: 但世代推移，軌憲時改，上元今古，考準或異，故三代課步，始卒各別。

translations.literal: But as generations shift, astronomical standards are revised from age to age; high origins of past and present and calibrations for verification may differ—therefore the calendrical steps of the three dynasties differ from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: But as generations pass, calendrical norms change with the times; high origins and verification standards differ between past and present, so the computational steps of the Three Dynasties vary from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 臣職預其事，而朽惰已甚，既謝運籌之能，彌愧意算之藝，由是多歷年世，茲業弗成，公私負責，俯仰慚靦。

translations.literal: Your servant's office participated in this matter, yet age and slackness have grown extreme; having already lost the skill of strategic reckoning, I am all the more ashamed before the art of mental calculation—hence many years and generations have passed and this task remains unfinished, a debt both public and private; looking up and down I burn with shame.
translations.idiomatic: Though my office has been involved, age and indolence have taken their toll; I no longer have the skill for strategic reckoning, and I am all the more ashamed of my deficiencies in computational arts. Years have piled up while the work remains unfinished—a debt owed both to the state and in private—and I am ashamed wherever I turn.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令曰：「可如所請。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "It may be as requested."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Let it be as requested."

sentences.zh: 延昌四年冬，太傅、清河王懌，司空、尚書令、任城王澄，散騎常侍、尚書僕射元暉，侍中、領軍、江陽王繼奏：「天道至遠，非人情可量；

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Yanbi, the Grand Tutor and Prince of Qinghe, Yi; the Minister of Works, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng; Regular Attendant of Fast Cavalry and Vice Director of the Secretariat, Yuan Hui; and Palace Attendant, Director of Palace Guards, and Prince of Jiangyang, Ji, submitted: "Heaven's Way is most remote—not what human sentiment can measure;
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yanchang year 4, Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe, Minister of Works and Secretariat Director Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Regular Attendant and Vice Director Yuan Hui, and Palace Attendant and Director of Palace Guards Prince Ji of Jiangyang submitted: "Heaven's Way is exceedingly remote—not something human feeling can gauge;

sentences.zh: 曆數幽微，豈以意輒度。

translations.literal: calendrical numbers are obscure and subtle—how can one arbitrarily estimate them by intent?
translations.idiomatic: calendrical reckonings are subtle and recondite—how can one simply guess at them by intuition?

sentences.zh: 而議者紛紜，競起端緒，爭指虛遠，難可求衷，自非建標準影，無以驗其真偽。

translations.literal: Yet discussants have been numerous and clamorous, each raising a thread of argument, contending over what is empty and distant with no means to find the center; unless one erects a standard and measures shadows, there is no way to test truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet debaters swarm with competing lines of argument, disputing over abstractions with no way to reach a fair judgment; unless one sets up a gnomon and measures shadows, there is no way to verify what is true or false.

sentences.zh: 頃永平中雖有考察之利，而不累歲窮究，遂不知影之至否，差失少多。

translations.literal: Recently, though there was benefit in the investigation during Yongping, because the inquiry was not carried through year by year, they still did not know whether the shadow measurements were correct or how much error there was more or less.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, during Yongping, investigation did yield some benefit, but because the inquiry was not pursued year after year to the end, no one knew whether the shadow readings were correct or how large the errors were.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，謂宜今年至日，更立表木，明伺晷度，三載之中，足知當否。

translations.literal: We your ministers have examined the matter and hold that at this year's winter solstice one should newly erect a gnomon post and clearly observe gnomon degrees; within three years it would suffice to know what is correct.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed the matter and believe that at this year's winter solstice a new gnomon post should be erected and gnomon shadow degrees carefully observed; within three years that would suffice to determine what is correct.

sentences.zh: 令是非有歸，爭者息競，然後採其長者，更議所從。」

translations.literal: Then right and wrong will have a basis, disputants will cease their competition, and afterward one may take what is strongest and deliberate afresh what to follow."
translations.idiomatic: Then right and wrong will have a clear basis, disputants will cease their quarrels, and afterward the strongest method can be chosen and a fresh decision made on which system to adopt."

sentences.zh: 神龜初，光復表曰：「春秋載『天子有日官，諸侯有日御』，又曰『履端于始』，『歸餘于終』，皆所以推二氣，考五運，成六位，定七曜，審八卦，立三才，正四序，以授百官于朝，萬民于野。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengui, Guang again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records 'The Son of Heaven has an officer of the sun, the feudal lords have sun keepers,' and also says 'Begin the year from the start' and 'Return the surplus at the end'—all are means to extrapolate the two qi, examine the five movements, complete the six positions, fix the seven luminaries, scrutinize the eight trigrams, establish the three powers, and set right the four seasons, so as to grant them to the hundred officials at court and the myriad people in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shengui era, Guang again submitted a memorial: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records that 'the Son of Heaven has a sun officer, and the feudal lords have sun stewards,' and also says 'take the beginning as the start' and 'return the surplus at the end'—all of this serves to extrapolate the two qi, examine the five phases, complete the six positions, fix the seven luminaries, scrutinize the eight trigrams, establish the three powers, and set the four seasons in order, so as to grant this to the hundred officials at court and the myriad people in the fields.

sentences.zh: 陰陽剛柔，仁義之道，罔不畢備。

translations.literal: Yin and yang, hard and soft, the Way of humaneness and righteousness—nothing is not fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang, firmness and yielding, and the Way of humaneness and righteousness—nothing is left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 由是先代重之，垂於典籍。

translations.literal: Hence former ages valued this and handed it down in the canonical records.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason former ages prized it and preserved it in the canonical records.

sentences.zh: 及史遷、班固、司馬彪著立書志，所論備矣。

translations.literal: When Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Sima Biao established their treatise-sections in writing, what they discussed was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Sima Biao composed their bibliographic treatises, their discussions were exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 謹案曆之作也，始自黃帝，辛卯為元，迄于大魏，甲寅紀首，十有餘代，歷祀數千，軌憲不等，遠近殊術。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the making of calendars: it began with the Yellow Emperor, with xinmao as the origin; down to Great Wei, with jiayin as the cycle head—more than ten generations, thousands of years of sacrificial service, unequal standards and remote or near different methods.
translations.idiomatic: A careful review shows that calendar-making began with the Yellow Emperor, with the xinmao origin; down to Great Wei, with the jiayin cycle head—more than ten dynasties and thousands of years of rites, with unequal standards and methods that differed widely in their assumptions.

sentences.zh: 其消息盈虛，覘步疏密，莫得而識焉。

translations.literal: Their waxing and waning, fullness and emptiness, observed steps loose or tight—none could be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Their waxing and waning, fullness and emptiness, and the tightness or looseness of their computational steps could not be fully understood.

sentences.zh: 去延昌四年冬，中堅將軍、屯騎校尉張洪，故太史令張明豫息盪寇將軍龍祥，校書郎李業興等三家並上新曆，各求申用。

translations.literal: Leaving the winter of the fourth year of Yanbi: Major General of the Central Fortitude and Commandant of Mounted Escort Zhang Hong; Longxiang, General Who Quells Bandits and son of the former Director of Astronomy Zhang Mingyu; and Proofreader Li Yexing—the three houses together submitted new calendars, each seeking adoption.
translations.idiomatic: As of the winter of Yanchang year 4, Major General and Commandant of Mounted Escort Zhang Hong; Longxiang, General Who Quells Bandits and son of the former Director of Astronomy Zhang Mingyu; and proofreader Li Yexing—three parties together submitted new calendars, each requesting official adoption.

sentences.zh: 臣學缺章程，藝謝籌運，而竊職觀閣，謬忝厥司，奏請廣訪諸儒，更取通數兼通經義者及太史，並集祕書，與史官同驗疏密，并請宰輔羣官臨檢得失，至於歲終，密者施用。

translations.literal: Your servant's learning lacks regulations and methods, my art falls short of reckoning and planning, yet I usurp my post to observe the archive and am unworthily entrusted with this office; I memorialize to widely consult the Confucian scholars, further take those who are broadly skilled in numbers and also understand the classics' meaning, together with the Directors of Astronomy, all assemble in the Secretariat, and with the historiographers jointly verify what is loose or tight; I also request that the chief ministers and all officials personally inspect strengths and weaknesses; by year's end, whatever is tight shall be put into use.
translations.idiomatic: My own learning lacks proper method, and my skill falls short of computational planning, yet I hold this office unworthily in the archive; I therefore request broad consultation with Confucian scholars, and the further selection of those skilled in numerology who also understand the classics, together with the Directors of Astronomy, all to assemble in the Secretariat and jointly test each system's precision with the historiographers; I also ask the chief ministers and officials to inspect the results in person, and by year's end whichever system proves tightest shall be adopted.

sentences.zh: 奉詔聽可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted approval.

sentences.zh: 時太傅、太尉公、清河王臣懌等以天道至遠，非卒可量，請立表候影，期之三載，乃採其長者，更議所從。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Prince of Qinghe, Lord Yi, and others, on the grounds that Heaven's Way is most remote and cannot be measured in short order, requested erection of a gnomon to await shadow measurement, with a term of three years, whereupon they would take what is strongest and deliberate afresh what to follow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Tutor and Grand Commandant Prince Yi of Qinghe and others, holding that Heaven's Way is too remote to be measured quickly, requested that a gnomon be erected to observe shadows, with a three-year term, after which the best method would be chosen and a fresh decision made on which system to follow.

sentences.zh: 又蒙敕許。

translations.literal: Again we received the gracious edict's assent.
translations.idiomatic: This too received the imperial assent.

sentences.zh: 於是洪等與前鎮東府長史祖瑩等研窮其事，爾來三年，再歷寒暑，積勤構思，大功獲成。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hong and the others, with the former chief secretary of the Eastern Military Staff of the Former Commandery, Zu Ying, and others deeply investigated the matter; since then three years have passed, twice experiencing cold and heat; accumulating diligence and framing thought, the great work was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Hong and the others, together with the former chief secretary of the Eastern Staff, Zu Ying, and others, pursued the matter to its depths; three years passed and two rounds of seasons elapsed before diligent labor and careful design at last brought the great work to completion.

sentences.zh: 謹案洪等三人前上之曆，并駙馬都尉盧道虔、前太極採材軍主衞洪顯、殄寇將軍太史令胡榮及雍州沙門統道融、司州河南人樊仲遵、定州鉅鹿人張僧豫所上，總合九家，共成一曆，元起壬子，律始黃鍾，考古合今，謂為最密。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the calendars previously submitted by Hong and the three men, together with those submitted by Commander of Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law Lu Daoqian; former Army Master of the Supreme Ultimate Talent Selection, Wei Hongxian; Director of Astronomy and General Who Exterminates Bandits Hu Rong; the monk leader Daorong of Yongzhou; Fan Zhongzun of Henan in Sizhou; and Zhang Sengyu of Julu in Dingzhou—in all nine houses combined into one calendar, origin beginning at renzi, pitch standards beginning at Yellow Bell, examining antiquity to accord with the present—we deem it the tightest.
translations.idiomatic: A careful review shows that the calendars previously submitted by Hong and his three colleagues, together with those of Commander of Horse Lu Daoqian; former Supreme Ultimate talent-selection army master Wei Hongxian; Director of Astronomy and General Who Exterminates Bandits Hu Rong; the monk leader Daorong of Yongzhou; Fan Zhongzun of Henan in Sizhou; and Zhang Sengyu of Julu in Dingzhou—in all nine parties—were combined into one calendar with the origin at renzi and pitch standards beginning at the Yellow Bell; comparing antiquity with the present, we judge it the most precise.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝元封中治曆，改年為太初，即名太初曆；

translations.literal: Formerly in the yuanfeng era of Han Emperor Wu the calendar was regulated and the era name was changed to Taichu—hence it was named the Taichu calendar;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, in the yuanfeng era of Han Emperor Wu, the calendar was revised and the era name changed to Taichu—it was therefore called the Taichu calendar;

sentences.zh: 魏文帝景初中治曆，即名景初曆。

translations.literal: in the jingchu era of Wei Emperor Wen the calendar was regulated—hence it was named the Jingchu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: in the jingchu era of Wei Emperor Wen the calendar was revised—it was therefore called the Jingchu calendar.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下道唯先天，功𨗿稽古，休符告徵，靈蔡炳瑞。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty's Way precedes Heaven alone; your achievements reach back to antiquity; blessed omens declare their signs; the sacred tortoise-shell and divining stalks shine with auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that Your Majesty's Way precedes Heaven itself, your achievements reach back to antiquity, blessed omens proclaim their signs, and the sacred tortoise and divining stalks blaze with auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 壬子北方，水之正位；

translations.literal: Renzi is the northern direction, water's correct position;
translations.idiomatic: Renzi is the northern direction, the proper position of water;

sentences.zh: 龜為水畜，實符魏德；

translations.literal: the tortoise is water's creature and truly accords with Wei's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: the tortoise is the creature of water and truly matches the Wei's Water Virtue;

sentences.zh: 修母子應，義當麟趾。

translations.literal: adjusting mother-and-child resonance, ritually right as the qilin's footprint.
translations.idiomatic: adjusting the resonance of mother and child pitch pipes, as ritually fitting as the qilin's footprint.

sentences.zh: 請定名為神龜曆。

translations.literal: We request that it be fixed and named the Shengui calendar.
translations.idiomatic: We request that it be formally named the Shengui calendar.

sentences.zh: 今封以上呈，乞付有司重加考議。

translations.literal: Now we seal and present it above, humbly asking that it be delivered to the relevant offices for renewed and added examination and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: We now seal and submit it for Your Majesty's review, humbly requesting that the relevant offices conduct further examination and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 事可施用，并藏祕府，附於典志。

translations.literal: If the matter may be put into use, let it also be stored in the secret archive and appended to the canonical treatises.
translations.idiomatic: If approved for use, let it also be stored in the secret archive and appended to the canonical treatises.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗以曆就，大赦改元，因名正光曆，班於天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong, because the calendar was complete, issued a general amnesty and changed the era name, naming the calendar the Zhengguang calendar, and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong, because the calendar was complete, issued a general amnesty and changed the era name; the calendar was named the Zhengguang calendar and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其九家共修，以龍祥、業興為主。

translations.literal: Of the nine houses who jointly compiled it, Longxiang and Yexing were the principals.
translations.idiomatic: Of the nine parties who jointly compiled it, Longxiang and Yexing served as the principal authors.

sentences.zh: 正光曆

translations.literal: The Zhengguang calendar
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengguang Calendar

sentences.zh: 壬子元以來，至今大魏正光三年歲在壬寅，積十六萬七千七百五十，算外；

translations.literal: From the renzi origin to the present, Great Wei Zhengguang year 3, the year being renyin—the accumulated count is 167,750, exclusive;
translations.idiomatic: From the renzi origin to the present, Great Wei Zhengguang year 3 (renyin)—the accumulated count is 167,750, exclusive;

sentences.zh: 壬子歲入甲申紀以來，至今孝昌二年歲在丙午，積四萬六千五百五十四，算外。

translations.literal: From the renzi year entering the jiashen cycle to the present, Xiaochang year 2, the year being bingwu—the accumulated count is 46,554, exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: From the renzi year entering the jiashen era cycle to the present, Xiaochang year 2 (bingwu)—the accumulated count is 46,554, exclusive.

sentences.zh: 從壬子元以來，至今大魏孝昌三年歲次丁未，積十六萬七千七百五十六，算上；

translations.literal: From the renzi origin to the present, Great Wei Xiaochang year 3, the year being dingwei—the accumulated count is 167,756, inclusive;
translations.idiomatic: From the renzi origin to the present, Great Wei Xiaochang year 3 (dingwei)—the accumulated count is 167,756, inclusive;

sentences.zh: 壬子歲入甲申紀以來，[1]至今大魏孝昌三年歲次丁未，積四萬六千五百五十六，算上。

translations.literal: From the renzi year entering the jiashen cycle to the present,[1] Great Wei Xiaochang year 3, the year being dingwei—the accumulated count is 46,556, inclusive.
translations.idiomatic: From the renzi year entering the jiashen era cycle to the present,[1] Great Wei Xiaochang year 3 (dingwei)—the accumulated count is 46,556, inclusive.

sentences.zh: 章歲，五百五。

translations.literal: Rule years, 505.
translations.idiomatic: Rule years: 505.

sentences.zh: 〈古十九年七閏，閏餘盡為章。

translations.literal: 〈In antiquity nineteen years and seven intercalations—the intercalary remainder entirely forms the rule.
translations.idiomatic: 〈In antiquity, nineteen years with seven intercalations—the intercalary remainder entirely constituted the rule.

sentences.zh: 積至多年，月盡之日，月見東方，日蝕先晦，輒復變曆，以同天象。

translations.literal: Accumulating over many years, on the day the month was exhausted the moon appeared in the east and eclipses preceded the new moon; then they would again alter the calendar to match the heavenly signs.
translations.idiomatic: Over many accumulated years, on the day the month ran out the moon would appear in the east and solar eclipses would precede the new moon; then the calendar would be revised again to match the heavenly signs.

sentences.zh: 二百年多一日，三百年多一日半，晦朔失。

translations.literal: Over two hundred years there is one extra day; over three hundred years one and a half extra days—new and full moon were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Over two hundred years the count ran one day long; over three hundred years, a day and a half—new and full moons fell out of alignment.

sentences.zh: 故先儒及緯文皆言「三百年斗曆改憲」。

translations.literal: Hence earlier Ruists and weft texts all say "Every three hundred years the Dipper calendar changes its standard."
translations.idiomatic: Hence earlier Confucian scholars and apocryphal texts all say, "Every three hundred years the Dipper calendar must change its standard."

sentences.zh: 候天減閏，五百五年減閏餘一，九千五百九十五年減一閏月，則從僖公五年至今，日蝕不失晦與二日，合朔者多。

translations.literal: Observing Heaven and reducing intercalations: every 505 years reduce the intercalary remainder by one; every 9,595 years reduce by one intercalary month—then from Duke Xi's fifth year to the present, solar eclipses miss neither the last day of the month nor the second day, and conjunctions of new moon match more often.
translations.idiomatic: By observing Heaven and reducing intercalations—subtracting one from the intercalary remainder every 505 years and one intercalary month every 9,595 years—from Duke Xi's fifth year to the present, solar eclipses rarely miss the last or second day of the month, and new-moon conjunctions match more closely.

sentences.zh: 閏餘成月，餘盡為章。〉

translations.literal: When the intercalary remainder completes a month, the remainder entirely forms the rule.〉
translations.idiomatic: When the intercalary remainder completes a month, the remainder entirely forms the rule.〉

sentences.zh: 章閏，一百八十六。

translations.literal: Rule intercalations, 186.
translations.idiomatic: Rule intercalations: 186.

sentences.zh: 〈五百五年閏月之數，其中減舊十九分之一。〉

translations.literal: 〈The number of intercalary months in 505 years, reduced therein by one-nineteenth of the old value.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The number of intercalary months in 505 years, reduced by one-nineteenth from the old value.〉

sentences.zh: 章月，六千二百四十六。

translations.literal: Rule months, 6,246.
translations.idiomatic: Rule months: 6,246.

sentences.zh: 〈五百五年所有月之數并閏月。〉

translations.literal: 〈The total number of all months in 505 years, including intercalary months.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The total number of months in 505 years, including intercalary months.〉

sentences.zh: 蔀法，六千六十。

translations.literal: Obscuration divisor, 6,060.
translations.idiomatic: Obscuration divisor: 6,060.

sentences.zh: 〈十二章為一蔀，至此年小餘成日，為度法。〉

translations.literal: 〈Twelve rules form one obscuration; when in that year the small remainder completes a day, it becomes the degree divisor.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twelve rules form one obscuration; when in that year the small remainder completes a day, it becomes the degree divisor.〉

sentences.zh: 斗分，一千四百七十七。

translations.literal: Dipper fraction, 1,477.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper fraction: 1,477.

sentences.zh: 〈四分度法得一千五百一十五，為古法。

translations.literal: 〈The quarter-degree divisor yields 1,515—that is the old method.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The quarter-degree divisor yields 1,515—that is the old method.

sentences.zh: 今減三十八者，從僖公五年以來減七日有奇，謂為最近。

translations.literal: Now reducing by thirty-eight: from Duke Xi's fifth year to the present, seven and a fraction days were reduced—we deem this nearest.
translations.idiomatic: The present reduction of thirty-eight reflects a reduction of seven and a fraction days since Duke Xi's fifth year—we deem this the closest fit.

sentences.zh: 一百一十三歲減□日，減之太深，是以三十餘年改徙四子也。〉

translations.literal: Reducing [one] day every 113 years—reducing too deeply, hence in little more than thirty years they changed and moved four origins.〉
translations.idiomatic: Reducing [one] day every 113 years cut too deeply, which is why in little more than thirty years they changed and shifted four origins.〉

sentences.zh: 紀法，六萬六百。

translations.literal: Era divisor, 60,600.
translations.idiomatic: Era divisor: 60,600.

sentences.zh: 〈十蔀成紀，大餘十也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Ten obscurations form an era; the big remainder is ten.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Ten obscurations form an era; the big remainder is ten.〉

sentences.zh: 統法，十二萬一千二百。

translations.literal: Concordance divisor, 121,200.
translations.idiomatic: Concordance divisor: 121,200.

sentences.zh: 〈二紀成統，大餘二十。〉

translations.literal: 〈Two eras form a concordance; the big remainder is twenty.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Two eras form a concordance; the big remainder is twenty.〉

sentences.zh: 元法，三十六萬三千六百。

translations.literal: Origin divisor, 363,600.
translations.idiomatic: Origin divisor: 363,600.

sentences.zh: 〈三統成元，大餘盡。〉

translations.literal: 〈Three concordances form an origin; the big remainder is exhausted.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Three concordances form an origin; the big remainder is exhausted.〉

sentences.zh: 日法，七萬四千九百五十二。

translations.literal: Day divisor, 74,952.
translations.idiomatic: Day divisor: 74,952.

sentences.zh: 〈十二乘章月為日法。

translations.literal: 〈Twelve times the rule months gives the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twelve times the rule months gives the day divisor.

sentences.zh: 章月，一年之閏分。〉

translations.literal: Rule months are one year's intercalary fraction.〉
translations.idiomatic: Rule months are one year's intercalary fraction.〉

sentences.zh: 周天分，二百二十一萬三千三百七十七。

translations.literal: Circuits-of-Heaven fraction, 2,213,377.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits-of-Heaven fraction: 2,213,377.

sentences.zh: 〈以度法通三百六十五度，內斗分。〉

translations.literal: 〈Using the degree divisor to convert 365 degrees, plus the Dipper fraction.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Using the degree divisor to convert 365 degrees, plus the Dipper fraction.〉

sentences.zh: 氣法，二十四。

translations.literal: Qi divisor, 24.
translations.idiomatic: Qi divisor: 24.

sentences.zh: 〈歲中十二，一年一十二次。

translations.literal: 〈Twelve mid-year qi in a year—twelve stations in a year.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twelve mid-year qi in a year—twelve lunar stations in a year.

sentences.zh: [2]次有初中，分為二十四。〉

translations.literal: [2] Each station has beginning and middle, divided into twenty-four.〉
translations.idiomatic: [2] Each station has a beginning and middle, divided into twenty-four.〉

sentences.zh: 經月，大餘二十九，小餘三萬九千七百六十九。

translations.literal: Canonical month: big remainder 29, small remainder 39,769.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical month: big remainder 29, small remainder 39,769.

sentences.zh: 〈日法除周天分得之。

translations.literal: 〈Obtained by dividing the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction by the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Obtained by dividing the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction by the day divisor.

sentences.zh: 日法者一蔀之月數，周天分者一蔀之日數。

translations.literal: The day divisor is the number of months in one obscuration; the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction is the number of days in one obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: The day divisor is the number of months in one obscuration; the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction is the number of days in one obscuration.

sentences.zh: 以蔀月除蔀日，[3]得一月二十九及餘，是周天分即為月通。〉

translations.literal: Dividing obscuration days by obscuration months, [3] one obtains twenty-nine months and a remainder—the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction is thus the month commonality.〉
translations.idiomatic: Dividing obscuration days by obscuration months, [3] one obtains twenty-nine months and a remainder—the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction is thus the month commonality.〉

sentences.zh: 會數，百七十三，餘二萬三千二百八。

translations.literal: Conjunction number, 173, remainder 23,208.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction number: 173, remainder 23,208.

sentences.zh: 〈五月二十三分月之二十為一會。

translations.literal: 〈Twenty parts of twenty-three months of five months form one conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twenty twenty-thirds of a month times five months form one conjunction.

sentences.zh: 以二十三乘五月，內二十，得一百三十五，以乘周天分。

translations.literal: Multiplying five months by twenty-three and adding twenty gives 135; multiply the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction by this.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying five months by twenty-three and adding twenty gives 135; multiply the Circuits-of-Heaven fraction by this.

sentences.zh: 以二十三乘日法除之，得一百七十三及餘。〉

translations.literal: Multiplying the day divisor by twenty-three and dividing, one obtains 173 and a remainder.〉
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying the day divisor by twenty-three and dividing, one obtains 173 and a remainder.〉

sentences.zh: 會通，一千二百九十八萬九千九百四。

translations.literal: Conjunction commonality, 1,298,999,904.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction commonality: 1,298,999,904.

sentences.zh: 〈以日法乘會數，內會餘。〉

translations.literal: 〈Multiplying the conjunction number by the day divisor and adding the conjunction remainder.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Multiplying the conjunction number by the day divisor and adding the conjunction remainder.〉

sentences.zh: 周日，二十七，餘四萬一千五百六十二。

translations.literal: Circuit day, 27, remainder 41,562.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit day: 27, remainder 41,562.

sentences.zh: 〈以月一日行除周天，得二十七日及餘。〉

translations.literal: 〈Dividing the Circuits of Heaven by the moon's one-day motion yields twenty-seven days and a remainder.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Dividing the Circuits of Heaven by the moon's daily motion yields twenty-seven days and a remainder.〉

sentences.zh: 通周，二百六萬五千二百六十六。

translations.literal: Common circuit, 2,065,266.
translations.idiomatic: Common circuit: 2,065,266.

sentences.zh: 〈日法乘周日二十七，內周餘。〉

translations.literal: 〈Multiplying circuit day twenty-seven by the day divisor and adding the circuit remainder.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Multiplying circuit day 27 by the day divisor and adding the circuit remainder.〉

sentences.zh: 小周，六千七百五十一。

translations.literal: Lesser circuit, 6,751.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser circuit: 6,751.

sentences.zh: 〈月一日行十三度，乘章歲，內章閏也。〉

translations.literal: 〈The moon's one-day motion of thirteen degrees, multiplied by rule years, plus rule intercalations.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The moon's daily motion of thirteen degrees, multiplied by rule years, plus rule intercalations.〉

sentences.zh: 月周，八萬一千一十二。

translations.literal: Lunar circuit, 81,012.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar circuit: 81,012.

sentences.zh: 〈以十二乘小周即得，與度同。〉

translations.literal: 〈Multiplying the lesser circuit by twelve gives this—it equals degrees.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Multiplying the lesser circuit by twelve gives this—it equals degrees.〉

sentences.zh: 推月朔術第一

translations.literal: Method I for calculating new moons
translations.idiomatic: Method I: Calculating New Moons

sentences.zh: 推積月術曰：置入紀年，算外，以章月乘之，如章歲為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for calculating accumulated months, it says: set the years since era entry, count exclusive, multiply by rule months, divide by rule years for accumulated months; what is not exhausted is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating accumulated months: set the years since era entry, count exclusive, multiply by rule months, divide by rule years to obtain accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalary remainder.

sentences.zh: 閏餘滿三百一十九以上，其歲有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder fills 319 or more, that year has an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary remainder reaches 319 or more, that year has an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 推朔積日術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分，分滿日法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for calculating accumulated new-moon days, it says: multiply accumulated months by the commonality number for accumulated new-moon parts; when the parts fill the day divisor they become accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating accumulated new-moon days: multiply accumulated months by the commonality number to obtain accumulated new-moon parts; when the parts fill the day divisor they become accumulated days; the remainder is the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from the accumulated days; what is not exhausted is the big remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Remove six decades from the accumulated days; the remainder is the big remainder.

sentences.zh: 命以紀，算外，則所求年天正十一月朔日。

translations.literal: Name it with the era cycle, count exclusive, and that is the new moon day of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Name it against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the new moon of the eleventh month of the civil year sought.

sentences.zh: 推上下弦望術曰：加朔大餘七、小餘二萬八千六百八十、小分一，小分滿四，從小餘；

translations.literal: Method for calculating first quarter, full moon, and last quarter, it says: add to the new moon's big remainder 7, small remainder 28,680, and small parts 1; when small parts fill four, carry to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating first quarter, full moon, and last quarter: add to the new moon's big remainder 7, small remainder 28,680, and small parts 1; when small parts fill four, carry to the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿日法，從大餘一；

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry one to the big remainder;
translations.idiomatic: when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry one to the big remainder;

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十，去之，即上弦日。

translations.literal: when the big remainder fills sixty, remove it—that is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: when the big remainder fills sixty, remove it—that is the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望；

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon;
translations.idiomatic: Add again to obtain the full moon;

sentences.zh: 又加，得下弦；

translations.literal: add again to obtain last quarter;
translations.idiomatic: add again to obtain the last quarter;

sentences.zh: 又加，得後月朔。

translations.literal: add again to obtain the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: add again to obtain the next month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術第二

translations.literal: Method II for calculating the twenty-four qi
translations.idiomatic: Method II: Calculating the Twenty-Four Qi

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術曰：置入紀年以來，算外，以餘數乘之為實。

translations.literal: Method for calculating the twenty-four qi, it says: set the years since era entry, count exclusive, multiply by the remainder number to obtain the dividend.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating the twenty-four qi: set the years since era entry, count exclusive, multiply by the remainder number for the dividend.

sentences.zh: 以蔀法除之，所得為積沒，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Divide it by the obscuration divisor; what is obtained is accumulated extinction; what is not exhausted is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by the obscuration divisor; the quotient is accumulated extinction, and the remainder is the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated extinction; what is not exhausted is the big remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Remove six decades from accumulated extinction; the remainder is the big remainder.

sentences.zh: 命以紀，算外，所求年天正十一月冬至日。

translations.literal: Name it by the era cycle, count exclusive: the winter solstice day of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Name it against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the winter solstice of the eleventh month of the civil year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五、小餘一千三百二十四、小分一，小分滿氣法二十四，從小餘一；

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add to the big remainder 15, to the small remainder 1,324, and to the small parts 1; when the small parts fill the qi divisor 24, carry 1 to the small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: For the next qi, add 15 to the big remainder, 1,324 to the small remainder, and 1 to the small parts; when small parts reach 24, carry 1 to the small remainder;

sentences.zh: 小餘滿蔀法，從大餘一；

translations.literal: when the small remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry 1 to the big remainder;
translations.idiomatic: when the small remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry 1 to the big remainder;

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十，去之，命如上，即次氣日。

translations.literal: when the big remainder fills sixty, remove it; name as above—that is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: when the big remainder reaches 60, drop a full cycle and name as before—that is the day of the next qi.

sentences.zh: 推閏術曰：以閏餘減章歲五百五，餘以歲中十二乘之。

translations.literal: Method for calculating intercalation, it says: subtract the intercalary remainder from rule years 505; multiply the remainder by year medians 12.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating intercalation: subtract the intercalary remainder from rule years 505, then multiply the remainder by 12 year medians.

sentences.zh: 滿章閏一百八十六，得一月；

translations.literal: when it fills rule intercalations 186, obtain one month;
translations.idiomatic: when the product fills rule intercalations 186, obtain one month;

sentences.zh: 餘半法已上，亦得一月。

translations.literal: if the remainder is at the half-divisor or above, likewise obtain one month.
translations.idiomatic: if the remainder is at or above half the divisor, likewise count one month.

sentences.zh: 數從天正十一月起，算外，閏月月也。

translations.literal: Count from Heaven's first month, month eleven, count exclusive: that is the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Count from the eleventh month of the civil year, count exclusive, and that is the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣為正。

translations.literal: Intercalations may advance or retreat; the standard is having no mid-climate.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalations may shift forward or back, but the governing rule is that the leap month contains no major solar term.

sentences.zh: 冬至十一月中 小寒十二月節 大寒十二月中 立春正月節

translations.literal: Winter Solstice: eleventh month, mid-month; Minor Cold: twelfth month, node; Major Cold: twelfth month, mid-month; Start of Spring: first month, node.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice — 11th month, major qi; Minor Cold — 12th month, minor qi; Major Cold — 12th month, major qi; Start of Spring — 1st month, minor qi.

sentences.zh: 雨水正月中 驚蟄二月節 春分二月中 清明三明節

translations.literal: Rain Water: first month, mid-month; Awakening of Insects: second month, node; Spring Equinox: second month, mid-month; Clear and Bright: third-month node.
translations.idiomatic: Rain Water — 1st month, major qi; Awakening of Insects — 2nd month, minor qi; Spring Equinox — 2nd month, major qi; Clear and Bright — third-month minor qi.

sentences.zh: 穀雨三月中 立夏四月節 小滿四月中 芒種五月節

translations.literal: Grain Rain: third month, mid-month; Start of Summer: fourth month, node; Minor Fullness: fourth month, mid-month; Grain in Ear: fifth month, node.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain — 3rd month, major qi; Start of Summer — 4th month, minor qi; Minor Fullness — 4th month, major qi; Grain in Ear — 5th month, minor qi.

sentences.zh: 夏至五月中 小暑六月節 大暑六月中 立秋七月節

translations.literal: Summer Solstice: fifth month, mid-month; Minor Heat: sixth month, node; Major Heat: sixth month, mid-month; Start of Autumn: seventh month, node.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice — 5th month, major qi; Minor Heat — 6th month, minor qi; Major Heat — 6th month, major qi; Start of Autumn — 7th month, minor qi.

sentences.zh: 處暑七月中 白露八月節 秋分八月中 寒露九月節

translations.literal: End of Heat: seventh month, mid-month; White Dew: eighth month, node; Autumn Equinox: eighth month, mid-month; Cold Dew: ninth month, node.
translations.idiomatic: End of Heat — 7th month, major qi; White Dew — 8th month, minor qi; Autumn Equinox — 8th month, major qi; Cold Dew — 9th month, minor qi.

sentences.zh: 霜降九月中 立冬十月節 小雪十月中 大雪十一月節

translations.literal: Frost Descent: ninth month, mid-month; Start of Winter: tenth month, node; Minor Snow: tenth month, mid-month; Major Snow: eleventh month, node.
translations.idiomatic: Frost Descent — 9th month, major qi; Start of Winter — 10th month, minor qi; Minor Snow — 10th month, major qi; Major Snow — 11th month, minor qi.

sentences.zh: 推交會術第三[4]

translations.literal: Method III for calculating nodal conjunction[4]
translations.idiomatic: Method III: Calculating Nodal Conjunction[4]

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕去交度術曰：置入紀朔積分，又以交會差分并之，今用甲申紀，差分七百四十一萬八千七百八十四也。
