translations.literal: Method for calculating degrees from the node at new-moon conjunction, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse, it says: set the accumulated new-moon fraction since era entry, and also add the conjunction–node difference parts; for the cycle now in use, Jiashen Cycle, the difference parts are 7,418,784.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating nodal distance at syzygy: set the accumulated new-moon fraction since era entry and add the conjunction–node difference parts; under the present Jiashen Cycle the difference parts are 7,418,784.

sentences.zh: 以會通去之，所得為積交，餘不盡者，以日法除之，所得為度餘，即所求年天正十一月朔却去交度及餘。

translations.literal: Remove what fills the conjunction communication constant; what is obtained is accumulated crossing; what of the remainder is not exhausted—divide by the day divisor—what is obtained is the degree remainder: the degrees and remainder by which the new moon of Heaven's first month, month eleven, stands back from the node in the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce modulo the conjunction communication constant for accumulated crossing; divide the remainder by the day divisor for the degree remainder—the degrees and parts by which the eleventh-month new moon precedes the node in the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月去交度術曰：加度二十九日、度餘三萬九千七百六十九，除如上，則次月去交度及分。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the next month's degrees from the node, it says: add 29 degrees and degree remainder 39,769; divide as above—then the next month's degrees from the node and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next month's nodal distance: add 29 days and degree remainder 39,769, reduce as above, and that gives the next month's distance from the node in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 求望去交度術曰：加度十四日、度餘五萬七千三百六十半，度餘滿日法從度，滿會數去之，亦除其餘；

translations.literal: Method for seeking full moon's degrees from the node, it says: add 14 degrees and degree remainder 57,360 and a half; when the degree remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the degrees; when it fills the conjunction number, remove it, and likewise divide the remainder;
translations.idiomatic: Method for full-moon nodal distance: add 14 days and 57,360½ degree parts; carry overflow at the day divisor and reduce modulo the conjunction number as before.

sentences.zh: 餘若不足減者，減度一，加會虛，則望去交度及分。

translations.literal: if the remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree and add the conjunction deficit—then the full moon's degrees from the node and parts.
translations.idiomatic: if the remainder cannot be reduced, borrow one degree and add the conjunction deficit to obtain full-moon nodal distance in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 朔望去交度分如朔望合數十四度、度餘五萬七千三百六十半已下，入交限數一百五十八度、度餘四萬七百九十九半以上者，朔則交會，望則月蝕。

translations.literal: If the new-moon and full-moon degrees and parts from the node are at or below the new-moon–full-moon conjunction number—14 degrees and degree remainder 57,360 and a half—and at or above the entry-into-crossing limit number—158 degrees and degree remainder 40,799 and a half—then at new moon there is nodal conjunction, and at full moon there is lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When syzygy nodal distance falls within the entry limit—no greater than the 14-day 57,360½ conjunction interval and no less than 158° 40,799½—new moon yields nodal conjunction and full moon yields lunar eclipse.

translations.idiomatic: 〈At new moon the sun and moon align like paired jade disks, with the crossing at center.〉

translations.idiomatic: Conjunction–node difference: 74 degrees, degree remainder 10,608.

sentences.zh: 求交道所在月：以十一月朔却去交度及餘，減會數及餘，餘若不足減者，減一度，加日法，[6]乃減之。

translations.literal: Method for finding the month in which the crossing falls: take the degrees and remainder by which the eleventh-month new moon stands back from the node, subtract the conjunction number and its remainder; if the remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree and add the day divisor,[6] then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: To find the month of nodal crossing: subtract the conjunction number and remainder from the eleventh-month new moon's nodal distance; if the remainder is insufficient, borrow one degree and add the day divisor,[6] then subtract.

sentences.zh: 乃以十一月朔小餘加之，滿日法，除去之，從日一，餘為日餘。

translations.literal: Then add to it the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; when it fills the day divisor, remove it and carry 1 to the days—the remainder is the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Then add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; carry at the day divisor for whole days, and the remainder is the day remainder.

sentences.zh: 命起往年十一月，如曆月大小除之，不滿月者為入月，算外，交道日。

translations.literal: Name starting from the eleventh month of the prior year; divide by long and short months as in the calendar—what does not fill a month is the month entered; count exclusive: the day of nodal crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Count from the prior year's eleventh month, divide by the calendar's long and short months; the partial month is the entered month, and counting exclusive gives the day of nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 交在望前者，其月朔則交會，望則月蝕；

translations.literal: If the crossing is before full moon, that month's new moon yields nodal conjunction, and full moon yields lunar eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: If the crossing precedes full moon, that month has nodal conjunction at new moon and lunar eclipse at full moon;

sentences.zh: 交在望後者亦其月月蝕，後月朔則交會。

translations.literal: if the crossing is after full moon, that month likewise has lunar eclipse, and the next month's new moon yields nodal conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: if the crossing follows full moon, that month has a lunar eclipse, and the following month's new moon yields nodal conjunction.

sentences.zh: 交正在望者，其月月蝕既，前後朔皆交會；

translations.literal: if the crossing falls exactly at full moon, that month has total lunar eclipse, and the new moons before and after both yield nodal conjunction;
translations.idiomatic: if the crossing falls exactly at full moon, that month has a total lunar eclipse, with nodal conjunction at the new moons on either side;

sentences.zh: 交正在朔者，日蝕既，前後望皆月蝕。

translations.literal: if the crossing falls exactly at new moon, there is total solar eclipse, and the full moons before and after both yield lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: if the crossing falls exactly at new moon, there is a total solar eclipse, with lunar eclipses at the full moons on either side.

sentences.zh: 求後交月及日：以會數及餘加前入月日及餘，餘滿日法，從日一，如曆月大小除之，命起前蝕月，得後交月及餘。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the month and day of the next crossing: add the conjunction number and its remainder to the prior entered month's days and remainder; when the remainder fills the day divisor, carry 1 to the days; divide by long and short months as in the calendar; name starting from the prior eclipse month—obtain the next crossing month and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next crossing month and day: add the conjunction number and remainder to the prior entered month and day, carry at the day divisor, divide by calendar months from the prior eclipse month, and obtain the next crossing month and remainder.

sentences.zh: 推月在日道表裏術曰：置入紀朔積分，又以紀交會差分加之，

translations.literal: Method for calculating whether the moon is outside or inside the solar path, it says: set the accumulated new-moon fraction since era entry, and also add the cycle's conjunction–node difference parts,
translations.idiomatic: Method for determining whether the moon lies north or south of the ecliptic: set the accumulated new-moon fraction since era entry and add the cycle's conjunction–node difference parts,

sentences.zh: 〈今用甲申紀[7]交會差分七百四十一萬八千七百八十四。〉

translations.literal: 〈For the cycle now in use, Jiashen Cycle[7], the conjunction–node difference parts are 7,418,784.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Under the present Jiashen Cycle[7], the conjunction–node difference parts are 7,418,784.〉

sentences.zh: 倍會通，去之。

translations.literal: Remove double multiples of the conjunction communication constant.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce modulo twice the conjunction communication constant.

sentences.zh: 餘不滿會通者：紀首裏者，則天正十一月合朔，月在日道裏；

translations.literal: If the remainder does not fill the conjunction communication constant: if the cycle head is inside, then at the eleventh-month conjunction of Heaven's first month the moon is inside the solar path;
translations.idiomatic: If the remainder is less than the conjunction communication constant: when the cycle opens inside, the eleventh-month new-moon moon lies inside the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 紀首表者，則月在表。

translations.literal: if the cycle head is outside, then the moon is outside.
translations.idiomatic: when the cycle opens outside, the moon lies outside the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 若滿會通者：紀首表者，則月在裏；

translations.literal: If it fills the conjunction communication constant: if the cycle head is outside, then the moon is inside;
translations.idiomatic: If the remainder fills the conjunction communication constant: when the cycle opens outside, the moon lies inside;

sentences.zh: 紀首裏者，則月在表。

translations.literal: if the cycle head is inside, then the moon is outside.
translations.idiomatic: when the cycle opens inside, the moon lies outside the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 黃道南為表，北為裏。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow Path is outside; north is inside.
translations.idiomatic: South of the ecliptic is outside; north is inside.

sentences.zh: 其滿會通者去之，餘如日法而一，即往年天正十一月朔却交度及餘。

translations.literal: Remove what fills the conjunction communication constant; divide the remainder by the day divisor to obtain one—this is the degrees and remainder by which the prior year's eleventh-month new moon stands back from the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Drop full conjunction communication constants and divide the remainder by the day divisor to obtain the prior year's eleventh-month new-moon nodal distance in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 以却去交度及餘減會數及會餘，會餘若不足減者，減一度，加日法乃減。

translations.literal: Subtract the degrees and remainder standing back from the crossing from the conjunction number and conjunction remainder; if the conjunction remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree and add the day divisor, then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract nodal distance from the conjunction number and remainder; if the conjunction remainder is insufficient, borrow one degree and add the day divisor before subtracting.

sentences.zh: 餘為前去度及餘。

translations.literal: The remainder is the prior forward degrees and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder is the forward nodal distance in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: [8]又以十一月朔小餘加之，滿日法從度一。

translations.literal: [8]Then add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; when it fills the day divisor, carry 1 to the degrees.
translations.idiomatic: [8]Then add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; carry one degree when the day divisor is filled.

sentences.zh: 命起十一月，如曆月大小除之，不滿月者為入月日及餘，算外，交道日。

translations.literal: Name starting from the eleventh month; divide by long and short months as in the calendar—what does not fill a month is the entered month, days, and remainder; count exclusive: the day of nodal crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Count from the eleventh month, divide by calendar months; the partial month gives the entered month, day, and remainder, and counting exclusive yields the day of nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 〈若十一月朔月在日道裏者，此交為出外，後交為入內；

translations.literal: 〈If at the eleventh-month new moon the moon is inside the solar path, this crossing is exiting outward and the next crossing is entering inward;
translations.idiomatic: 〈If the eleventh-month new moon lies inside the ecliptic, this crossing exits outward and the next enters inward;

sentences.zh: 十一月朔在表者，此交為入內，後交為出外。

translations.literal: if the eleventh-month new moon is outside, this crossing is entering inward and the next crossing is exiting outward.
translations.idiomatic: if the eleventh-month new moon lies outside the ecliptic, this crossing enters inward and the next exits outward.

sentences.zh: 一出一入，常法也。〉

translations.literal: One exit and one entry—this is the constant rule.〉
translations.idiomatic: One exit and one entry—this is the standing rule.〉

sentences.zh: 其交在朔後望前者，朔，月在日道表裏與十一月同，望則反矣。

translations.literal: If the crossing falls after new moon and before full moon, at new moon the moon's position outside or inside the solar path is the same as in the eleventh month, but at full moon it is reversed.
translations.idiomatic: If the crossing falls between new moon and full moon, the moon at new moon matches the eleventh month's inside/outside polarity, but at full moon the polarity reverses.

sentences.zh: 若交在望後朔前者，望與十一月同，後月朔則異矣。

translations.literal: If the crossing falls after full moon and before the next new moon, full moon matches the eleventh month, but the next month's new moon differs.
translations.idiomatic: If the crossing falls between full moon and the next new moon, full moon matches the eleventh month, but the following new moon differs.

sentences.zh: 〈若先交會後月蝕者，朔，月在日道裏；

translations.literal: 〈If nodal conjunction precedes lunar eclipse, at new moon the moon is inside the solar path;
translations.idiomatic: 〈When nodal conjunction precedes lunar eclipse, at new moon the moon lies inside the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 望，在表。

translations.literal: at full moon, it is outside.
translations.idiomatic: at full moon it lies outside.

sentences.zh: 朔在表，則望在裏。

translations.literal: If at new moon it is outside, then at full moon it is inside.
translations.idiomatic: If new moon is outside, full moon is inside.

sentences.zh: 其先月蝕後交會者，望在表則朔在裏也。〉

translations.literal: If lunar eclipse precedes nodal conjunction, if at full moon it is outside then at new moon it is inside.〉
translations.idiomatic: When lunar eclipse precedes nodal conjunction, outside at full moon means inside at new moon.〉

sentences.zh: 望在裏則朔在表矣。

translations.literal: If at full moon it is inside, then at new moon it is outside.
translations.idiomatic: Inside at full moon means outside at new moon.

sentences.zh: 推交會起角術曰：其月在外道，先會後交者，虧從東南角起；

translations.literal: Method for calculating the starting corner of nodal conjunction, it says: if that month is on the outer path, when conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the southeast corner;
translations.idiomatic: Method for the eclipse starting corner: when the moon is on the outer path and conjunction precedes crossing, obscuration begins at the southeast limb;

sentences.zh: 先交後會者，虧從西南角起。

translations.literal: when crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: when crossing precedes conjunction, obscuration begins at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 其月在內道，先會後交者，虧從西北角起；

translations.literal: If that month is on the inner path, when conjunction precedes crossing, the waning begins from the northwest corner;
translations.idiomatic: When the moon is on the inner path and conjunction precedes crossing, obscuration begins at the northwest limb;

sentences.zh: 先交後會者，虧從西北角起。

translations.literal: when crossing precedes conjunction, the waning begins from the northwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: when crossing precedes conjunction, obscuration begins at the northwest limb.

sentences.zh: 合交中者，蝕之既。

translations.literal: When conjunction and crossing coincide at center, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: When syzygy and nodal crossing coincide at center, the eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕在日之衝，起角亦如之。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse, the moon stands opposite the sun, and the starting corner follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: At lunar eclipse the moon stands opposite the sun, and the starting corner follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 推蝕分多少術曰：置入交限十五度，以朔望去交日數減之，餘則蝕分。

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘術曰：以入曆日餘乘所入曆下損益率，以小周六千七百五十一除之，所得以損益盈縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: Method for calculating the fixed large and small remainders for conjunction, node crossing, and lunar eclipse, it says: multiply the day remainder entered into the table by the damage-benefit rate below that table entry; divide by the small cycle 67,051; take what is obtained to damage or benefit the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts—this is the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Method for fixing conjunction, nodal, and eclipse remainders: multiply the anomalistic day remainder by the tabulated excess-deficit rate, divide by 67,051, and apply the result to the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts to obtain the fixed accumulated parts.

sentences.zh: [27]值盈者，以減本朔望小餘；

translations.literal: [27]Where the value is surplus, subtract from the original new-moon and full-moon small remainder;
translations.idiomatic: [27]When the result is surplus, subtract it from the base syzygy small remainder;

sentences.zh: 值縮者，加之。

translations.literal: Where the value is shrinkage, add to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the result is deficit, add it to the base syzygy small remainder.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法者，[28]交會加時在後日。

translations.literal: If adding fills the day divisor, [28] the nodal-crossing hour-mark falls on the following day.
translations.idiomatic: If the addition fills the day divisor, [28] the nodal-crossing hour falls on the next day.

sentences.zh: 減之，不足減者，減上一日，加下日法乃減之，交會加時在前日。

translations.literal: Subtract it; if insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the upper day, add the day divisor below, then subtract; the nodal-crossing hour-mark falls on the prior day.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract it; if the remainder is insufficient, borrow one day from the upper count, add the day divisor, then subtract—the nodal-crossing hour falls on the previous day.

sentences.zh: 月蝕者，隨定大小餘為定日加時。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse, follow the fixed large and small remainders to obtain the fixed day hour-mark.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipse, take the fixed large and small remainders as the fixed day and hour.

sentences.zh: 推加時術曰：以時法六千二百四十六除定小餘，所得命以子起，算外。

translations.literal: Method for calculating the hour-mark, it says: divide the fixed small remainder by the hour divisor 6,246; name what is obtained starting from zi, count exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating the hour-mark: divide the fixed small remainder by the hour divisor, 6,246; name the result starting from zi (midnight), count exclusive.

sentences.zh: 朔望加時有餘不盡者，四之，如法得一為少，[29]二為半，三為太半。

translations.literal: When the syzygy hour-mark has remainder not exhausted, quadruple it; as one per divisor gives minor, [29] two gives half, three gives major half.
translations.idiomatic: When the syzygy hour-mark leaves a remainder, quadruple it; one per divisor is "minor," [29] two is "half," three is "major half."

sentences.zh: 又有餘者，三之，如法得一為強，半法以上排成之，不滿半法棄之。

translations.literal: If there is further remainder, triple it; as one per divisor gives strong; at half divisor and above, round up to one; below half divisor, discard.
translations.idiomatic: If a remainder still remains, triple it; one per divisor is "strong"; at or above half the divisor, round up; below half the divisor, discard.

sentences.zh: 以強并少為少強，并半為半強，并太為太強，得二強者為少弱，以之并少為半強，[30]以之并半為太弱。

translations.literal: Combining strong with minor makes minor-strong; with half makes half-strong; with major makes major-strong; two strongs make minor-weak; combining that with minor makes half-strong, [30] combining with half makes major-weak.
translations.idiomatic: Combine "strong" with "minor" to get "minor-strong," with "half" for "half-strong," with "major" for "major-strong"; two "strongs" make "minor-weak"; combine that with "minor" for "half-strong," [30] with "half" for "major-weak."

sentences.zh: 以之并太為一弱，隨所在辰命之，則其強弱。

translations.literal: Combining that with major makes one-weak; name it according to the double-hour where it stands, and that is its strong-weak grade.
translations.idiomatic: Combine that with "major" for "one-weak"; name it against the double-hour in which it falls, and that gives its strength grade.

sentences.zh: 日之衝為破，月常在破下蝕。

translations.literal: The sun's diametric point is po (break); the moon is always eclipsed beneath po.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's opposition point is po (break); the moon is always eclipsed below it.

sentences.zh: 入曆值周日者術曰：以周日日餘乘損率，[31]以周日度小分并。

translations.literal: Method when entry into the table hits circuit day, it says: multiply circuit-day day remainder by damage rate, [31] add circuit-day degree small parts.
translations.idiomatic: Method when anomalistic entry falls on circuit day: multiply the circuit-day day remainder by the damage rate, [31] and add the circuit-day degree small parts.

sentences.zh: 又以入曆日餘乘之為實，以小周乘周日日餘為法，實如法得一，以減縮積積分。

translations.literal: Also multiply again by day remainder entered into the table for dividend; multiply lesser cycle by circuit-day day remainder for divisor; one per divisor from dividend, subtract from shrinkage accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply again by the anomalistic day remainder for the dividend; multiply the lesser cycle by the circuit-day day remainder for the divisor; take one per divisor from the dividend and subtract from the shrinkage accumulated parts.

sentences.zh: 有餘者，以加本朔望小餘，小餘滿日法從大餘一，是為蝕後日。

translations.literal: If there is remainder, add to original syzygy small remainder; when small remainder fills day divisor carry 1 to big remainder—this is the day after eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If a remainder remains, add it to the base syzygy small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry 1 to the big remainder—this is the day after the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推加時如上法。

translations.literal: Calculate the hour-mark by the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate the hour-mark by the method above.

sentences.zh: 推日月合朔弦望度術第五

translations.literal: Method V for calculating sun and moon conjunction, new moon, quarter, and full moon degrees
translations.idiomatic: Method V: Calculating Sun and Moon Degrees at Conjunction, Quarters, and Full Moon

sentences.zh: 推日度術曰：置入紀朔積日，以日度法乘之，滿周天去之，餘滿日度法為度，不盡為餘。

translations.literal: Method for calculating solar degree, it says: set accumulated new-moon days since era entry; multiply by solar-degree divisor; when filling circuit heaven remove; when remainder fills solar-degree divisor it becomes degrees; not exhausted is remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating solar longitude: set the accumulated new-moon days since era entry, multiply by the solar-degree divisor, remove circuit heaven when filled; the quotient in solar-degree divisors is degrees, the remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命度起牛前十二度，

translations.literal: Name the degrees starting from twelve degrees before Ox,
translations.idiomatic: Name the degrees starting twelve degrees before Ox,

sentences.zh: 〈牛前十二度，在斗十五度也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Twelve degrees before Ox—that is fifteen degrees into Dipper.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twelve degrees before Ox—that is fifteen degrees into Dipper.〉

sentences.zh: 宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即天正十一月朔夜半日所在度。

translations.literal: Remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, count exclusive—that is the degree where the sun stands at midnight new moon of Heaven's first month, month eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Remove by lodge sequence; count exclusive at the partial lodge, and that gives the sun's degree at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh month of the civil year.

sentences.zh: 推日度又法，術曰：置周天三百六十五度、斗分一千四百七十七，以冬至去朔日數減一，餘以減周天度，冬至小餘減斗分，不足減者，減度一，加日度法，乃減之。

translations.literal: Another method for calculating solar degree, it says: set circuit heaven 365 degrees and Dipper fraction 1,477; subtract one from the number of days from winter solstice back to new moon; subtract the remainder from circuit-heaven degrees; subtract Dipper fraction from winter-solstice small remainder; if insufficient to subtract, subtract one degree, add solar-degree divisor, then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate method for solar longitude: set circuit heaven at 365 degrees and Dipper fraction 1,477; subtract one from the days from winter solstice to new moon, subtract that from circuit-heaven degrees, and subtract the Dipper fraction from the winter-solstice small remainder; if insufficient, borrow one degree, add the solar-degree divisor, then subtract.

sentences.zh: 命起如上，即所求年天正十一月朔日夜半日所在度。

translations.literal: Name starting as above—that is midnight new moon solar degree of the year sought, Heaven's first month, month eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Name starting as above, and that gives the sun's degree at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh month of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月日所在度術曰：月大加三十度，月小加二十九度，求次日加一度，宿次除之，逕斗去其分一千四百七十七。

translations.literal: Method for next month's solar degree, it says: big month add 30 degrees, small month add 29 degrees; for next day add 1 degree; remove by lodge sequence; passing Dipper remove its fraction 1,477.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next month's solar degree: add 30 degrees in a long month, 29 in a short month; add 1 degree for the next day; remove by lodge sequence; when passing Dipper, subtract its extra fraction of 1,477.

sentences.zh: 推合朔日月共度術曰：以章歲乘朔小餘，以章月除之，所得為大分，不盡為小分，[32]以加夜半日度分，分滿日度法從度，命起如前，即所求年天正十一月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: Method for calculating conjunction shared sun-moon degree, it says: multiply new-moon small remainder by rule years; divide by rule months; what is obtained is big parts, not exhausted is small parts, [32] add to midnight solar degree parts; when parts fill solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; name starting as before—that is shared sun-moon degree at conjunction of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the shared sun-moon degree at conjunction: multiply the new-moon small remainder by rule years and divide by rule months; the quotient is big parts, the remainder small parts; [32] add these to the midnight solar degree parts, carrying to degrees when parts fill the solar-degree divisor; name as before, and that gives the shared sun-moon degree at the eleventh-month conjunction of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月合朔共度術曰：加度二十九、大分三千二百一十五、小分二千四百五十五，小分滿章月從大分，大分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，逕斗除其分，則次月合朔日月共度。

translations.literal: Method for next month's conjunction shared degree, it says: add 29 degrees, big parts 3,215, small parts 2,455; when small parts fill rule months carry to big parts; when big parts fill solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; remove by lodge sequence; passing Dipper remove its fraction—then next month's conjunction shared sun-moon degree.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next month's shared conjunction degree: add 29 degrees, 3,215 big parts, and 2,455 small parts; carry from small parts to big parts when they fill rule months, and from big parts to degrees when they fill the solar-degree divisor; remove by lodge sequence and subtract Dipper's extra fraction—the result is the next month's shared sun-moon degree at conjunction.

sentences.zh: 推月度術曰：置入紀朔積日，以月周八萬一千一十二乘之，滿周天去之，餘以日度法約之為度，不盡為度分。

translations.literal: Method for calculating lunar degree, it says: set accumulated new-moon days since era entry; multiply by lunar circuit 81,012; when filling circuit heaven remove; reduce remainder by solar-degree divisor for degrees; not exhausted is degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Method for lunar longitude: set the accumulated new-moon days since era entry, multiply by the lunar circuit 81,012, remove circuit heaven when filled, and reduce the remainder by the solar-degree divisor for degrees; the remainder is degree parts.

sentences.zh: 命度起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Name degrees starting from twelve degrees before Ox; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, count exclusive—that is degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight new moon of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Name degrees starting twelve degrees before Ox, remove by lodge sequence, count exclusive at the partial lodge, and that gives the moon's degree and parts at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh month of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 推月度又一法，術曰：以小周乘朔小餘為實，以章歲乘日法為法，實如法得一為度；

translations.literal: Another method for calculating lunar degree, it says: multiply new-moon small remainder by lesser cycle for dividend; multiply rule years by day divisor for divisor; one per divisor from dividend gives degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Alternate method for lunar longitude: multiply the new-moon small remainder by the lesser cycle for the dividend and rule years by the day divisor for the divisor; one per divisor from the dividend gives degrees;

sentences.zh: 不滿法者，以章月除之，為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: What does not fill the divisor, divide by rule months for big parts; not exhausted is small parts.
translations.idiomatic: What does not fill the divisor, divide by rule months for big parts; the remainder is small parts.

sentences.zh: [33]所得以減合朔度及分，餘即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: [33]Take what is obtained to subtract from conjunction degree and parts; remainder is degree and parts where the moon stands at midnight new moon of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: [33]Subtract the result from the conjunction degree and parts; the remainder is the moon's degree and parts at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh month of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次月度術曰：小月加度二十二、分二千六百五十一，大月加度三十五、分四千八百八十三，分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，[34]次月所在度。

translations.literal: Method for next month's lunar degree, it says: small month add 22 degrees, parts 2,651; big month add 35 degrees, parts 4,883; when parts fill solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, count exclusive, [34] next month's degree.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next month's lunar degree: add 22 degrees and 2,651 parts in a short month, 35 degrees and 4,883 parts in a long month; carry to degrees when parts fill the solar-degree divisor; remove by lodge sequence and count exclusive at the partial lodge—[34] that is the next month's degree.

sentences.zh: 求次日月行度術曰：加度十三、分二千二百三十二，分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，逕斗去其分。

translations.literal: Method for next day's lunar travel degree, it says: add 13 degrees, parts 2,232; when parts fill solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; remove by lodge sequence; passing Dipper remove its fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next day's lunar travel: add 13 degrees and 2,232 parts; carry to degrees when parts fill the solar-degree divisor; remove by lodge sequence and subtract Dipper's extra fraction.

sentences.zh: 求弦望日所在度術曰：加合朔度七、大分二千三百一十八、小分五千二百九十八、微分一，微分滿四從小分，小分滿章月從大分，大分滿日度法從度，命如上，則上弦日所在度。

translations.literal: Method for quarter and full moon solar degree, it says: add to conjunction degree 7, big parts 2,318, small parts 5,298, minute parts 1; when minute parts fill four carry to small parts; when small parts fill rule months carry to big parts; when big parts fill solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; name as above—then first-quarter solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: Method for solar longitude at quarter and full moon: add to the conjunction degree 7 degrees, 2,318 big parts, 5,298 small parts, and 1 minute part; carry from minute parts to small parts when they fill four, from small parts to big parts when they fill rule months, and from big parts to degrees when they fill the solar-degree divisor; name as above, and that gives the sun's degree at first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加得望、上弦、次月合朔。

translations.literal: Adding again gives full moon, last quarter, and next month's conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's conjunction.

translations.literal: Editorial note thirty-five in the degree-calculation procedures.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note thirty-five in the degree-calculation procedures.

sentences.zh: 斗二十六度 牛八度 女十二度 虛十度

translations.literal: Dipper 26 degrees, Ox 8 degrees, Woman 12 degrees, Void 10 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper: 26 degrees; Ox: 8 degrees; Woman: 12 degrees; Void: 10 degrees.

sentences.zh: 危十七度 室十六度 壁九度

translations.literal: Rooftop 17 degrees, House 16 degrees, Wall 9 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Rooftop: 17 degrees; House: 16 degrees; Wall: 9 degrees.

sentences.zh: 北方玄武七宿：九十八度一千四百七十七分

translations.literal: Northern Black Tortoise seven lodges: 98 degrees, 1,477 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Black Tortoise—seven lodges: 98 degrees, 1,477 parts.

sentences.zh: 奎十六度 婁十二度 胃十四度 昴十一度

translations.literal: Legs 16 degrees, Bond 12 degrees, Stomach 14 degrees, Hairy Head 11 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Legs: 16 degrees; Bond: 12 degrees; Stomach: 14 degrees; Hairy Head: 11 degrees.

sentences.zh: 畢十六度 觜二度 參九度

translations.literal: Net 16 degrees, Turtle Beak 2 degrees, Three Stars 9 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Net: 16 degrees; Turtle Beak: 2 degrees; Three Stars: 9 degrees.

sentences.zh: 西方白虎七宿：八十度

translations.literal: Western White Tiger seven lodges: 80 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Western White Tiger—seven lodges: 80 degrees.

sentences.zh: 井三十三度 鬼四度 柳十五度 星七度

translations.literal: Well 33 degrees, Ghost 4 degrees, Willow 15 degrees, Star 7 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Well: 33 degrees; Ghost: 4 degrees; Willow: 15 degrees; Star: 7 degrees.

sentences.zh: 張十八度 翼十八度 軫十七度

translations.literal: Extended Net 18 degrees, Wings 18 degrees, Chariot Base 17 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Extended Net: 18 degrees; Wings: 18 degrees; Chariot Base: 17 degrees.

sentences.zh: 南方朱鳥七宿：一百一十二度

translations.literal: Southern Vermilion Bird seven lodges: 112 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Vermilion Bird—seven lodges: 112 degrees.

sentences.zh: 角十二度 亢九度 氐一十五度 房五度

translations.literal: Horn 12 degrees, Neck 9 degrees, Root 15 degrees, Room 5 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Horn: 12 degrees; Neck: 9 degrees; Root: 15 degrees; Room: 5 degrees.

sentences.zh: 心五度 尾十八度 箕十一度

translations.literal: Heart 5 degrees, Tail 18 degrees, Winnowing Basket 11 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Heart: 5 degrees; Tail: 18 degrees; Winnowing Basket: 11 degrees.

sentences.zh: 東方倉龍七宿：七十五度

translations.literal: Eastern Azure Dragon seven lodges: 75 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Azure Dragon—seven lodges: 75 degrees.

sentences.zh: 周天三百六十五度、六千六十分度之一千四百七十七。

translations.literal: Circuit heaven: 365 degrees, 1,477 six-thousand-sixtieths of a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit heaven: 365 degrees and 1,477 parts in 6,060 parts of a degree.

sentences.zh: 通分，得二百二十一萬三千七百七十七，名曰周天分。

translations.literal: Common denominator conversion: obtain 2,213,777, called circuit-heaven parts.
translations.idiomatic: Convert to a common denominator to obtain 2,213,777, called circuit-heaven parts.

sentences.zh: 五行沒滅易卦氣候上朔術第六

translations.literal: Method VI for calculating five phases, extinction and submersion days, Book of Changes hexagrams, climate pentads, and upper new moon
translations.idiomatic: Method VI: Calculating the Five Phases, Extinction and Submersion Days, Hexagrams, Climate Pentads, and Upper New Moon

sentences.zh: 推五行用事日：水、火、木、金、土各王七十三日、小餘二百九十五、小分九、微分三，春木、夏火、秋金、冬水四立即其用事。

translations.literal: Calculate five-phase domain days: Water, Fire, Wood, Metal, and Earth each reign 73 days, small remainder 295, small parts 9, minute parts 3; Wood in spring, Fire in summer, Metal in autumn, Water in winter—the four establishments are their domains.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the days when the five phases hold sway: Water, Fire, Wood, Metal, and Earth each reign for 73 days, 295 small remainder, 9 small parts, and 3 minute parts; Wood in spring, Fire in summer, Metal in autumn, and Water in winter take domain at the four establishment days.

sentences.zh: 始求土者，置立春大小餘及分，以木王七十三日、小餘二百九十五、小分九、微分三加之，微分滿五從小分一，小分滿氣法二十四從小餘一，小餘滿蔀法從大餘一，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，得季春土王日。

translations.literal: To seek Earth first: set Establishment of Spring big and small remainders and parts; add Wood's reign 73 days, small remainder 295, small parts 9, minute parts 3; when minute parts fill five carry 1 to small parts; when small parts fill qi divisor 24 carry 1 to small remainder; when small remainder fills obscuration divisor carry 1 to big remainder; when big remainder fills 60 remove; name by era cycle—obtain late-spring Earth-reign day.
translations.idiomatic: To find Earth first: set the Establishment of Spring remainders and parts, add Wood's reign of 73 days, 295 small remainder, 9 small parts, and 3 minute parts; carry from minute parts to small parts when they fill five, from small parts to small remainder when they fill the qi divisor 24, and from small remainder to big remainder when they fill the obscuration divisor; remove sixty-day cycles from the big remainder and name against the era cycle to obtain the late-spring Earth-reign day.

sentences.zh: 又加土王十八日、小餘一千五百八十八、小分二十、微分二，滿從命如上，即得立夏日。

translations.literal: Also add Earth reign 18 days, small remainder 1,588, small parts 20, minute parts 2; when filled carry and name as above—then obtain Establishment of Summer day.
translations.idiomatic: Then add Earth's reign of 18 days, 1,588 small remainder, 20 small parts, and 2 minute parts; carry and name as above to obtain the Establishment of Summer day.

sentences.zh: 求次如法。

translations.literal: Seek the next by the same method.
translations.idiomatic: Find each subsequent day by the same method.

sentences.zh: 又一法求土王用事日：各置四立大小餘及分，各減大餘十八、小餘一千五百八十八、小分二十、微分二，命以紀，算外，即四立土王日。

translations.literal: Another method to seek Earth-reign domain day: for each set the four establishments' big and small remainders and parts; for each subtract big remainder 18, small remainder 1,588, small parts 20, minute parts 2; name by era cycle, count exclusive—that is Earth-reign day at the four establishments.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate method for the Earth-reign domain days: set the remainders and parts for each of the four establishment days, subtract 18 from the big remainder, 1,588 from the small remainder, 20 small parts, and 2 minute parts; name against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the Earth-reign day at each establishment.

sentences.zh: 若大餘不足減者，加六十而後減之；

translations.literal: If the big remainder is insufficient to subtract, add 60 and then subtract;
translations.idiomatic: If the big remainder is insufficient, add 60 and then subtract;

sentences.zh: 小餘不足減者，減取大餘一，加蔀法乃減之。

translations.literal: if the small remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the big remainder, add obscuration divisor, then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: if the small remainder is insufficient, borrow one from the big remainder, add the obscuration divisor, then subtract.

sentences.zh: 推沒滅術曰：因冬至積沒有小餘者，加積一，以沒分乘之，如沒法而一，為積日，不盡為沒餘。

translations.literal: Method for calculating extinction and submersion days, it says: from winter solstice, if accumulated submersion has small remainder, add 1 to accumulation; multiply by submersion parts; one per submersion divisor gives accumulated days; not exhausted is submersion remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Method for extinction and submersion days: from the winter solstice, if the accumulated submersion has a small remainder, add 1 to the accumulation; multiply by submersion parts and divide by the submersion divisor for accumulated days; the remainder is the submersion remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，餘為沒日，命以紀，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至後沒日。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; remainder is submersion day; name by era cycle, count exclusive—that is submersion day after winter solstice of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Remove six-day decades from the accumulated days; name the remainder against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the first submersion day after the winter solstice of the eleventh month of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求次沒術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘二萬七百六十四，沒餘滿沒法三萬一千七百七從沒日一，沒日滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次沒日。

translations.literal: Method for next submersion day, it says: add submersion day 69, submersion remainder 20,764; when submersion remainder fills submersion divisor 31,707 carry 1 to submersion day; when submersion day fills 60 remove; name by era cycle, count exclusive—that is next submersion day.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the next submersion day: add 69 submersion days and 20,764 to the submersion remainder; carry 1 to submersion days when the remainder fills the submersion divisor 31,707; remove sixty-day cycles from submersion days; name against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the next submersion day.

sentences.zh: [36]一歲常有五沒或六沒，小餘盡者為滅日。

translations.literal: [36]In one year there are usually five or six submersion days; when the small remainder is exhausted it is an extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: [36]A year usually has five or six submersion days; when the small remainder is exhausted, that day is an extinction day.

sentences.zh: 又，以冬至去朔日加沒日，冬至小餘滿蔀法從沒日，命日起天正十一月，如曆月大小除之，不足，除者入月算，命以朔，算外，即冬至後沒日。

translations.literal: Also: add submersion days to days from winter solstice back to new moon; when winter-solstice small remainder fills obscuration divisor carry to submersion days; name days starting Heaven's first month, month eleven; divide by calendar long and short months as usual; what does not fill, count entered month; name from new moon, count exclusive—that is submersion day after winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Also: add the submersion days to the days from winter solstice to new moon, carrying to submersion days when the winter-solstice small remainder fills the obscuration divisor; count from the eleventh month of the civil year and divide by long and short months as in the calendar; what does not fill a month enters the month count; name from the new moon, count exclusive, and that gives the submersion day after the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次沒：加沒沒日六十九，沒餘三千九百五十九、沒分二萬四千六百九十七，分滿沒法從沒餘，沒餘滿蔀法從沒日，[37]命起前沒月，曆月大小除之，[38]即後沒日及餘。

translations.literal: Seek next submersion: add submersion day 69, submersion remainder 3,959, submersion parts 24,697; when parts fill submersion divisor carry to submersion remainder; when submersion remainder fills obscuration divisor carry to submersion day, [37] name starting from prior submersion month; divide by calendar long and short months, [38] then later submersion day and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Find the next submersion: add 69 submersion days, 3,959 to the submersion remainder, and 24,697 submersion parts; carry from parts to submersion remainder when they fill the submersion divisor, and from submersion remainder to submersion days when it fills the obscuration divisor; [37] count from the month of the prior submersion and divide by long and short months—[38] that gives the next submersion day and remainder.

sentences.zh: 推四正卦術曰：因冬至大小餘，即坎卦用事日；

translations.literal: Method for calculating four standstill hexagrams, it says: from winter solstice big and small remainders—that is Kan hexagram domain day;
translations.idiomatic: Method for the four standstill hexagrams: from the winter solstice remainders, that is the day when the Kan hexagram holds sway;

sentences.zh: 春分，即震卦用事日；

translations.literal: spring equinox—that is Zhen hexagram domain day;
translations.idiomatic: the spring equinox is the day when the Zhen hexagram holds sway;

sentences.zh: 夏至，即離卦用事日；

translations.literal: summer solstice—that is Li hexagram domain day;
translations.idiomatic: the summer solstice is the day when the Li hexagram holds sway;

sentences.zh: 秋分，即兌卦用事日。

translations.literal: autumn equinox—that is Dui hexagram domain day.
translations.idiomatic: the autumn equinox is the day when the Dui hexagram holds sway.

sentences.zh: 求中孚卦：加冬至小餘五千五百三十、小分九、微分一，微分滿五從小分，小分滿氣法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，命以紀，算外，即中孚卦用事日。

translations.literal: Seek Zhongfu hexagram: add to winter-solstice small remainder 5,530, small parts 9, minute parts 1; when minute parts fill five carry to small parts; when small parts fill qi divisor carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills obscuration divisor carry to big remainder; name by era cycle, count exclusive—that is Zhongfu hexagram domain day.
translations.idiomatic: Find the Zhongfu hexagram: add 5,530 to the winter-solstice small remainder, 9 small parts, and 1 minute part; carry from minute parts to small parts when they fill five, from small parts to small remainder when they fill the qi divisor, and from small remainder to big remainder when it fills the obscuration divisor; name against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the day when Zhongfu holds sway.

sentences.zh: 其解加震，咸加離，賁加兌，亦如中孚加坎。

translations.literal: For it: Jie adds to Zhen, Xian adds to Li, Bi adds to Dui—likewise as Zhongfu adds to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: For Jie add to Zhen, for Xian add to Li, for Bi add to Dui—by the same rule as Zhongfu added to Kan.

sentences.zh: 求次卦：加坎大餘六、小餘五百二十九、小分十四、微分四，微分滿五從小分，小分滿氣法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，命以紀，算外，即復卦用事日。

translations.literal: Seek next hexagram: add to Kan big remainder 6, small remainder 529, small parts 14, minute parts 4; when minute parts fill five carry to small parts; when small parts fill qi divisor carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills obscuration divisor carry to big remainder; name by era cycle, count exclusive—that is Fu hexagram domain day.
translations.idiomatic: Find the next hexagram: add 6 to Kan's big remainder, 529 to the small remainder, 14 small parts, and 4 minute parts; carry as above; name against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the day when Fu holds sway.

sentences.zh: 大壯加震，姤加離，觀加兌，如中孚加坎。

translations.literal: Dazhuang adds to Zhen, Gou adds to Li, Guan adds to Dui—as Zhongfu adds to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhuang adds to Zhen, Gou adds to Li, Guan adds to Dui—by the same rule as Zhongfu added to Kan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，未濟、蹇、頤、中孚、復；

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Weiji, Jian, Yi, Zhongfu, Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Weiji, Jian, Yi, Zhongfu, Fu;

sentences.zh: 十二月，屯、謙、睽、升、臨；

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Tun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, Lin;
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Tun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, Lin;

sentences.zh: 正月，小過、蒙、益、漸、泰；

translations.literal: First month: Xiaoguo, Meng, Yi, Jian, Tai;
translations.idiomatic: First month: Xiaoguo, Meng, Yi, Jian, Tai;

sentences.zh: 二月，需、隨、晉、解、大壯；

translations.literal: Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, Dazhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, Dazhuang;

sentences.zh: 三月，訟、豫、蠱、革、夬；

translations.literal: Third month: Song, Yu, Gu, Ge, Guai;
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Song, Yu, Gu, Ge, Guai;

sentences.zh: 四月，旅、師、比、小畜、乾；

translations.literal: Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiaoxu, Qian;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiaoxu, Qian;

sentences.zh: 五月，大有、家人、井、咸、始；

translations.literal: Fifth month: Dayou, Jiaren, Jing, Xian, Shi;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Dayou, Jiaren, Jing, Xian, Shi;

sentences.zh: 六月，鼎、豐、渙、履、遯；

translations.literal: Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, Dun;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, Dun;

sentences.zh: 七月，恒、節、同人、損、否；

translations.literal: Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tongren, Sun, Pi;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tongren, Sun, Pi;

sentences.zh: 八月，巽、萃、大畜、賁、觀；

translations.literal: Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Daxu, Bi, Guan;
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Daxu, Bi, Guan;

sentences.zh: 九月，歸妹、无妄、明夷、困、剝；

translations.literal: Ninth month: Guimei, Wuwang, Mingyi, Kun, Bo;
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Guimei, Wuwang, Mingyi, Kun, Bo;

sentences.zh: 十月，艮、既濟、噬嗑、大過、坤。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Gen, Jiji, Shike, Daguo, Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: Gen, Jiji, Shike, Daguo, Kun.

sentences.zh: 四正為方伯，中孚為三公，復為天子，屯為諸侯，謙為大夫，暌為九卿，升還從三公，周而復始。

translations.literal: Four standstills serve as regional lords; Zhongfu as Three Dukes; Fu as Son of Heaven; Tun as feudal lords; Qian as grand masters; Kui as nine ministers; Sheng returns following Three Dukes, cycling repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The four standstill hexagrams correspond to regional lords; Zhongfu to the Three Dukes; Fu to the Son of Heaven; Tun to feudal lords; Qian to grand masters; Kui to the nine ministers; Sheng returns in the train of the Three Dukes, and the cycle begins anew.

sentences.zh: 九三應上九，清淨微溫陽風；

translations.literal: Nine-three responding to upper nine: clear and pure, slightly warm, yang wind;
translations.idiomatic: When line nine-three responds to upper nine: clear skies, slight warmth, and a yang wind;

sentences.zh: 九三應上六，絳赤決溫陰雨。

translations.literal: Nine-three responding to upper six: deep red, decisively warm, yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: When line nine-three responds to upper six: deep red skies, decidedly warm, with yin rain.

sentences.zh: 六三應上六，白濁微寒陰雨；

translations.literal: Six-three responding to upper six: white turbid, slightly cold, yin rain;
translations.idiomatic: When line six-three responds to upper six: white and murky, slightly cold, with yin rain;

sentences.zh: 六三應上九，麴塵決寒陽風。

translations.literal: Six-three responding to upper nine: yeast-dust, decisively cold, yang wind.
translations.idiomatic: When line six-three responds to upper nine: yeast-colored dust, decidedly cold, with a yang wind.

sentences.zh: 諸卦上有陽爻者，陽風；

translations.literal: For hexagrams with yang line above, yang wind;
translations.idiomatic: When a hexagram has a yang line on top, expect a yang wind;

sentences.zh: 上有陰爻者，陰雨。

translations.literal: with yin line above, yin rain.
translations.idiomatic: when a yin line is on top, expect yin rain.

sentences.zh: 推七十二候術曰：因冬至大小餘，即虎始交日，加大餘五、小餘四百四十一、小分八、微分一，微分滿三從小分，小分滿氣法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，[39]命以紀，算外，所候日。

translations.literal: Method for calculating seventy-two climate pentads, it says: from winter solstice big and small remainders—that is day when tigers begin mating; add big remainder 5, small remainder 441, small parts 8, minute parts 1; when minute parts fill three carry to small parts; when small parts fill qi divisor carry to small remainder; when small remainder fills obscuration divisor carry to big remainder, [39] name by era cycle, count exclusive—the pentad day.
translations.idiomatic: Method for the seventy-two climate pentads: from the winter solstice remainders, that is the day when tigers begin mating; add 5 to the big remainder, 441 to the small remainder, 8 small parts, and 1 minute part; carry as above; [39] name against the era cycle, count exclusive, and that gives the pentad day.

sentences.zh: 冬至 虎始交 芸始生 荔挺出

translations.literal: Winter Solstice: tigers begin mating, cress begins to sprout, iris sprouts emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice: tigers begin mating; cress begins to sprout; iris sprouts emerge.

sentences.zh: 小寒 蚯蚓結 麋角解 水泉動

translations.literal: Lesser Cold: earthworms form knots, elk antlers shed, spring waters stir.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Cold: earthworms coil; elk antlers shed; spring waters stir.

sentences.zh: 大寒 雁北向 鵲始巢 雉始雊

translations.literal: Greater Cold: wild geese turn north, magpies begin nesting, pheasants first crow.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Cold: wild geese turn north; magpies begin nesting; pheasants first crow.

sentences.zh: 立春 鷄始乳 東風解凍 蟄蟲始振

translations.literal: Establishment of Spring: hens begin brooding, east wind melts ice, hibernating insects first stir.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment of Spring: hens begin brooding; the east wind melts the ice; hibernating insects first stir.

sentences.zh: 雨水 魚上冰 獺祭魚 鴻雁來

translations.literal: Rain Water: fish ascend the ice, otters sacrifice fish, wild swans arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Rain Water: fish rise beneath the ice; otters offer fish; wild swans arrive.

sentences.zh: 驚蟄 始雨水 桃始華 倉庚鳴

translations.literal: Awakening of Insects: rain water begins, peach first blooms, orioles call.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of Insects: rain water begins; peach first blooms; orioles call.

sentences.zh: 春分 鷹化鳩 玄鳥至 雷始發聲

translations.literal: Spring Equinox: hawks transform to cuckoos, dark birds arrive, thunder first sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Spring Equinox: hawks turn to cuckoos; dark swallows arrive; thunder first sounds.

sentences.zh: 清明 電始見 蟄蟲咸動 蟄蟲啟戶

translations.literal: Clear and Bright: lightning first appears, hibernating insects all stir, hibernating insects open their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and Bright: lightning first appears; hibernating insects all stir; hibernating insects open their doors.

sentences.zh: 穀雨 桐始花 田鼠化為鴽[40] 虹始見

translations.literal: Grain Rain: paulownia first blooms, field mice transform to quail[40], rainbow first appears.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain: paulownia first blooms; field mice transform into quail[40]; the rainbow first appears.

sentences.zh: 立夏 萍始生 戴勝降於桑 螻蟈鳴

translations.literal: Establishment of Summer: duckweed first sprouts, hoopoes alight on mulberry, tree frogs call.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment of Summer: duckweed first sprouts; hoopoes alight on mulberry trees; tree frogs call.

sentences.zh: 小滿 蚯蚓出 王瓜生 苦菜秀

translations.literal: Lesser Fullness of Grain: earthworms emerge, snake gourds grow, sow thistles flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Fullness of Grain: earthworms emerge; snake gourds grow; sow thistles flourish.

sentences.zh: 芒種 靡草死 小暑至 螳蜋生

translations.literal: Grain in Beard: withering grasses die, Lesser Heat arrives, mantises hatch.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in Beard: withering grasses die; Lesser Heat arrives; mantises hatch.

sentences.zh: 夏至 鵙始鳴 反舌無聲 鹿角解

translations.literal: Summer Solstice: shrikes first call, mockingbirds fall silent, deer antlers shed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice: shrikes first call; mockingbirds fall silent; deer antlers shed.

sentences.zh: 小暑 蟬始鳴 半夏生 木槿榮

translations.literal: Lesser Heat: cicadas first chirp, pinellia sprouts, hibiscus blooms.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Heat: cicadas first chirp; pinellia sprouts; hibiscus blooms.

sentences.zh: 大暑 溫風至 蟋蟀居壁 鷹乃學習

translations.literal: Greater Heat: warm winds arrive, crickets retreat to walls, hawks begin training their young.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Heat: warm winds arrive; crickets retreat to walls; hawks begin training their young.

sentences.zh: 立秋 腐草化螢 土潤溽暑 涼風至

translations.literal: Establishment of Autumn: rotting grass becomes fireflies, earth moistens in humid heat, cool winds arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment of Autumn: rotting grass becomes fireflies; the earth moistens in humid heat; cool winds arrive.

sentences.zh: 處暑 白露降 寒蟬鳴 鷹祭鳥

translations.literal: End of Heat: white dew descends, cold cicadas chirp, hawks sacrifice birds.
translations.idiomatic: End of Heat: white dew descends; cold cicadas chirp; hawks sacrifice birds.

sentences.zh: 白露 天地始肅 暴風至 鴻雁來

translations.literal: White Dew: heaven and earth begin to chill, gales arrive, wild swans come.
translations.idiomatic: White Dew: heaven and earth begin to chill; gales arrive; wild swans come.

sentences.zh: 秋分 玄鳥歸 羣鳥養羞 雷始收聲

translations.literal: Autumn Equinox: dark swallows return, flocks of birds store provisions, thunder first falls silent.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Equinox: dark swallows return; flocks of birds store provisions; thunder first falls silent.

sentences.zh: 寒露 蟄蟲附戶 殺氣浸盛 陽氣始衰

translations.literal: Cold Dew: hibernating creatures cling to doors, killing qi gradually swells, yang qi begins to wane.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Dew: hibernating creatures cling to doors; killing qi gradually swells; yang qi begins to wane.

sentences.zh: 霜降 水始涸 鴻雁來賓 雀入大水化為蛤

translations.literal: Frost Descent: waters first dry up, wild swans arrive as guests, sparrows entering great waters transform into clams.
translations.idiomatic: Frost Descent: waters first dry up; wild swans arrive as guests; sparrows entering great waters transform into clams.

sentences.zh: 立冬 菊有黃華 豺祭獸 水始冰

translations.literal: Establishment of Winter: chrysanthemums show yellow blooms, jackals sacrifice game, water first freezes.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment of Winter: chrysanthemums show yellow blooms; jackals sacrifice game; water first freezes.

sentences.zh: 小雪 地始凍 雉入大水化為蜃 虹藏不見

translations.literal: Lesser Snow: earth first freezes, pheasants entering great waters transform into oysters, rainbows hide from view.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Snow: earth first freezes; pheasants entering great waters transform into oysters; rainbows hide from view.

sentences.zh: 大雪 冰益壯 地始坼 鶡旦不鳴

translations.literal: Greater Snow: ice grows stronger, earth first splits, crossbill-hawks at dawn cease calling.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Snow: ice grows stronger; earth first splits; crossbill-hawks at dawn cease calling.

sentences.zh: 術曰：因冬至虎始交後，五日一候。

translations.literal: The method says: from after the winter solstice pentad when tigers begin mating, one climate pentad every five days.
translations.idiomatic: The method says: from after the winter solstice pentad when tigers begin mating, there is one climate pentad every five days.

sentences.zh: 推上朔法：置入紀年減一，加八，以六律乘之，以六十去之，[41]餘為大餘，以甲子算外，上朔日。

translations.literal: Method for calculating upper new moon: set era-entry years minus one, add eight, multiply by the six pitch pipes, remove by sixty, [41] remainder is big remainder, count exclusive from jiazi—that is the upper new moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Method for calculating the upper new moon: set era-entry years minus one, add eight, multiply by the six pitch pipes, and remove by sixty; [41] the remainder is the big remainder—count exclusive from jiazi, and that gives the upper new moon day.

sentences.zh: 推五星六通術第七

translations.literal: Method VII for Calculating the Five Planets and the Six Passages
translations.idiomatic: Method VII: Calculating the Five Planets and the Six Passages

sentences.zh: 上元壬子以來至春秋隱公元年己未，積十六萬六千五百七，算外；

translations.literal: From upper origin renzi to the first year of Duke Yin of Spring and Autumn, year jiwei—the accumulated count is 166,507, exclusive;
translations.idiomatic: From the renzi upper origin to the first year of Duke Yin of Spring and Autumn, year jiwei, the accumulated count is 166,507, exclusive;

sentences.zh: 至今大魏熙平二年，歲次丁酉，積十六萬七千七百四十五，算外。

translations.literal: To the present Great Wei's Xiping year two, cyclical year dingyou—the accumulated count is 167,745, exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: To the present, Great Wei Xiping year 2, cyclical year dingyou, the accumulated count is 167,745, exclusive.

sentences.zh: 木精曰歲星，其數二百四十一萬六千六百六十。

translations.literal: The essence of Wood is called the Year Star; its number is 2,416,660.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Wood is the Year Star; its number is 2,416,660.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑，[42]其數四百七十二萬五千八百四十八。

translations.literal: The essence of Fire is called Dazzling Delusion, [42] its number is 4,725,848.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Fire is Dazzling Delusion; [42] its number is 4,725,848.

sentences.zh: 土精曰鎮星，其數二百二十九萬一千二十一。

translations.literal: The essence of Earth is called Quelling Star; its number is 2,291,021.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Earth is Quelling Star; its number is 2,291,021.

translations.literal: Editorial note forty-three in the five-planet procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note forty-three in the five-planet procedure.

sentences.zh: 金精曰太白，其數三百五十三萬八千一百三十一。

translations.literal: The essence of Metal is called Great White; its number is 3,538,131.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Metal is Great White; its number is 3,538,131.

sentences.zh: 水精曰辰星，其數七十萬二千一百八十二。

translations.literal: The essence of Water is called Chronogram Star; its number is 702,182.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Water is Chronogram Star; its number is 702,182.

sentences.zh: 推五星：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，以周天二百二十一萬三千三百七十七乘之，名為六通之實。

translations.literal: Calculating the five planets: set years from upper origin through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by circuit heaven 2,213,377—this is called the six-passage dividend.
translations.idiomatic: To calculate the five planets: set the years from the upper origin through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by circuit heaven, 2,213,377, and call the result the six-passage dividend.

sentences.zh: 以蔀法除之，所得為冬至積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Divide by obscuration divisor; what is obtained is accumulated winter-solstice days, what is not exhausted is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by the obscuration divisor; the quotient is accumulated winter-solstice days, the remainder the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘，命以甲子，算外，即冬至日。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what is not exhausted is big remainder; name from jiazi, count exclusive—that is the winter solstice day.
translations.idiomatic: Remove six decades from the accumulated days; the remainder is the big remainder—name from jiazi, count exclusive, and that gives the winter solstice day.

sentences.zh: 以章歲五百五除冬至小餘，所得命子，算外，即律氣加時。

translations.literal: Divide winter-solstice small remainder by rule years 505; name what is obtained from zi, count exclusive—that is the pitch-qi hour-mark.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the winter-solstice small remainder by rule years, 505; name the result from zi (midnight), count exclusive, and that gives the pitch-qi hour-mark.

sentences.zh: 五星各以其數為法，除六通實，所得為積合，不盡為合餘。

translations.literal: Each of the five planets uses its number as divisor; divide the six-passage dividend; what is obtained is accumulated conjunction, what is not exhausted is conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet uses its own number as divisor to divide the six-passage dividend; the quotient is accumulated conjunction, the remainder conjunction remainder.

sentences.zh: 以合餘減法，餘為入歲度分，以日度約之，所得即所求天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及餘。

translations.literal: Subtract conjunction remainder from divisor; remainder is degrees entered into the year; reduce by solar-degree divisor; what is obtained is dawn-and-dusk conjunction degree count and remainder after winter solstice of Heaven's first month, month eleven, of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the divisor; the remainder is the degree-fraction entered into the year—reduce by the solar-degree divisor, and the result is the dawn-and-dusk conjunction degree count and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 其金、水，以一合日數及合餘減合度算及餘，得一者為夕見，無所得為晨見。

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, subtract single-conjunction day number and conjunction remainder from conjunction degree count and remainder; if one is obtained, evening appearance; if nothing is obtained, morning appearance.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, subtract the single-conjunction day number and conjunction remainder from the conjunction degree count and remainder; a quotient of one means evening appearance, none means morning appearance.

sentences.zh: 若度餘不足減，減合度算一，加日度法乃減之。

translations.literal: If degree remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from conjunction degree count, add solar-degree divisor, then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: If the degree remainder is insufficient, borrow one from the conjunction degree count, add the solar-degree divisor, then subtract.

sentences.zh: 命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度及餘。

translations.literal: Name starting from twelve degrees before Ox; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, count exclusive—that is dawn-and-dusk conjunction degree and remainder after winter solstice of Heaven's first month, month eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Name starting twelve degrees before Ox, remove by lodge sequence, count exclusive at the partial lodge, and that gives the dawn-and-dusk conjunction degree and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求星合月及日：置冬至朔日數減一，以加合度算，以冬至小餘加度餘，度餘滿日度法去之，加度一，合度算變成合日算，餘為日餘。

translations.literal: Seek planet-conjunction month and day: set winter-solstice new-moon day number minus one, add to conjunction degree count; add winter-solstice small remainder to degree remainder; when degree remainder fills solar-degree divisor remove it and add one degree; conjunction degree count becomes conjunction day count, remainder is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the planet-conjunction month and day: set the winter-solstice new-moon day number minus one and add it to the conjunction degree count; add the winter-solstice small remainder to the degree remainder; when the degree remainder fills the solar-degree divisor, remove it and carry one degree—the conjunction degree count becomes the conjunction day count, and the remainder is the day remainder.

sentences.zh: 命起天正十一月，如曆月大小除之，不滿月者，算外，星合月及日，有閏計之。

translations.literal: Name starting Heaven's first month, month eleven; divide by calendar long and short months as usual; what does not fill a month, count exclusive—planet-conjunction month and day; if there is intercalation, account for it.
translations.idiomatic: Name starting from the eleventh month of the civil year, divide by long and short months as in the calendar, count exclusive at the partial month, and that gives the planet-conjunction month and day—account for intercalation when present.

sentences.zh: 求後合月及日：以合終日數及餘如前入月算及餘，餘滿日度從日，曆月大小除之，起前合月，算外，即後合月及日。

translations.literal: Seek next conjunction month and day: use conjunction terminal day number and remainder as before to enter month count and remainder; when remainder fills solar-degree divisor carry to days; divide by calendar long and short months; start from prior conjunction month, count exclusive—that is next conjunction month and day.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next conjunction month and day: add the conjunction terminal day number and remainder to the entered month count and remainder as before; carry to days when the remainder fills the solar-degree divisor; divide by long and short months; start from the prior conjunction month, count exclusive, and that gives the next conjunction month and day.

sentences.zh: 其金、水，以一合日數及餘，加晨得夕，加夕得晨。

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, with single-conjunction day number and remainder: add to morning to obtain evening, add to evening to obtain morning.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, add the single-conjunction day number and remainder—adding to morning appearance yields evening appearance, and adding to evening yields morning.

sentences.zh: 求後合度：以行星度及餘加前合度算及餘，餘滿日度從度，命起前合度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即後合度及餘。

translations.literal: Seek next conjunction degree: add planetary degree and remainder to prior conjunction degree count and remainder; when remainder fills solar-degree divisor carry to degrees; name starting from prior conjunction degree; remove by lodge sequence; what does not fill a lodge, count exclusive—that is next conjunction degree and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the next conjunction degree: add the planetary degree and remainder to the prior conjunction degree count and remainder; carry to degrees when the remainder fills the solar-degree divisor; name from the prior conjunction degree, remove by lodge sequence, count exclusive at the partial lodge, and that gives the next conjunction degree and remainder.

translations.idiomatic: When passing Dipper, subtract its extra fraction of 1,477.

translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow: nine parts per day, nine degrees in fifty-seven days, then it stops.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度。

translations.idiomatic: [44] It halts again for twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 復順，遲，日行九分，五十七日行九度。

translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow again: nine parts per day, nine degrees in fifty-seven days.

translations.idiomatic: Quelling Star: conjunction terminal days 378, terminal day remainder 341, planetary motion 12 degrees, degree remainder 4,924, circuit void 5,719.

translations.idiomatic: Quelling Star: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears behind the sun; after eighteen days plus day remainder 170½ and two degrees plus remainder 2,462, it reappears in the east at dawn, fifteen and a half degrees from the sun.

translations.literal: Prograde: daily motion one part in twelve; in eighty-four days it moves seven degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde: one part in twelve per day, seven degrees in eighty-four days, then it stops.

translations.idiomatic: It remains motionless for thirty-six days, then reverses.

translations.idiomatic: It halts again for thirty-six days.

translations.idiomatic: Prograde again at one part in twelve per day, seven degrees in eighty-four days; standing ahead of the sun, it disappears in the west.

translations.idiomatic: Damage 732: all editions wrongly read 一 for 二; emended by recalculation.

translations.idiomatic: 109 parts: all editions wrongly read 二 for 一; emended by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 縮積分七千二百七十二 諸本「二百」訛「一百」，今據校算改正。

translations.literal: Shrinkage accumulated parts 7,272: all editions wrongly read "one hundred" for "two hundred"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shrinkage accumulated parts 7,272: all editions wrongly read 一百 for 二百; emended by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 縮積分一萬九千三百九 諸本「三百九」訛「三百七」，今據校算改正。

translations.literal: Shrinkage accumulated parts 19,309: all editions wrongly read "307" for "309"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shrinkage accumulated parts 19,309: all editions wrongly read 三百七 for 三百九; emended by recalculation.

translations.literal: 392 parts: all editions wrongly read "two hundred" for "three hundred"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: 392 parts: all editions wrongly read 二百 for 三百; emended by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 縮積分二萬九千二百四十四 諸本「二百」訛「一百」，今據校算改正。

translations.literal: Shrinkage accumulated parts 29,244: all editions wrongly read "one hundred" for "two hundred"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shrinkage accumulated parts 29,244: all editions wrongly read 一百 for 二百; emended by recalculation.

translations.idiomatic: 243 parts: all editions wrongly read 三十三 for 四十三; emended by recalculation.
