translations.literal: 287 parts: all editions wrongly read "three hundred" for "two hundred"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: 287 parts: all editions wrongly read 三百 for 二百; emended by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 三百一十二分 諸本「一十二」訛「一十一」，今據校算改正。

translations.literal: 312 parts: all editions wrongly read "eleven" for "twelve"; emended by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: 312 parts: all editions wrongly read 一十一 for 一十二; emended by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 縮積分一萬一千五十八 諸本原均闕「一千」兩字，今據校算補。

translations.literal: Shrinkage accumulated parts 11,058: all editions originally lacked the two characters "one thousand"; supplied by recalculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shrinkage accumulated parts 11,058: all editions originally lacked 一千; supplied by recalculation.

sentences.zh: 為定積分 諸本「為定積分」上有「加之」兩字。

translations.literal: Fixed accumulated parts: all editions have the two characters "add to" above "fixed accumulated parts."
translations.idiomatic: Fixed accumulated parts: all editions have 加之 above 為定積分.

sentences.zh: 按上既云「所得以損益盈縮積分」，則下不當再云「加之」。

translations.literal: The text above already says "take what is obtained to damage or benefit the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts," so below it should not again say "add to."
translations.idiomatic: The text above already says "take what is obtained to damage or benefit the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts," so below it should not again say "add to."

sentences.zh: 本曆推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘術襲自景初諸曆，術文也基本相同，此句見宋書卷一二、卷一三曆志，景初、元嘉皆作「以損益盈縮積分為定積分」。

translations.literal: This calendar's method for fixing syzygy, nodal, and eclipse large and small remainders derives from the Jingchu and related calendars; the procedure text is essentially identical. This line appears in Song Shu calendar treatises, vols. 12–13; both Jingchu and Yuanjia read "take the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts damaged or benefited as the fixed accumulated parts."
translations.idiomatic: This calendar's method for fixing syzygy, nodal, and eclipse remainders derives from the Jingchu and related calendars; the procedure text is essentially identical. This line appears in Song Shu calendar treatises, vols. 12–13; both Jingchu and Yuanjia read "take the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts damaged or benefited as the fixed accumulated parts."

sentences.zh: 此處「加之」兩字顯衍，今刪。

translations.literal: The two characters "add to" here are clearly redundant; deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The two characters "add to" here are clearly redundant; deleted.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法者 諸本脫「加之」兩字，今參照景初、元嘉術補。

translations.literal: When adding fills the day divisor: all editions omit the two characters "add to"; supplied with reference to the Jingchu and Yuanjia procedures.
translations.idiomatic: When adding fills the day divisor: all editions omit 加之; supplied with reference to the Jingchu and Yuanjia procedures.

sentences.zh: 如法得一為少 諸本「如」作「加」。

translations.literal: As one per divisor gives minor: all editions read "add" for "as."
translations.idiomatic: As one per divisor gives minor: all editions read 加 for 如.

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷三０云：「加當作如。

translations.literal: Qian's Collation Notes, vol. 30, say: "Add should read as.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's Collation Notes, vol. 30, say: "Add should read as.

sentences.zh: 」錢說是，今據改。

translations.literal: " Qian's view is correct; changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian's view is correct; changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 以之并少為半強 諸本「之」作「定」。

translations.literal: Combine it with minor for half-strong: all editions read "fixed" for "it."
translations.idiomatic: Combine it with minor for half-strong: all editions read 定 for 之.

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷三０云：「定當作之。

translations.literal: Qian's Collation Notes, vol. 30, say: "Fixed should read it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's Collation Notes, vol. 30, say: "Fixed should read it.

sentences.zh: 」錢說是，今據改。

translations.literal: " Qian's view is correct; changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian's view is correct; changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 以周日日餘乘損率 諸本「日餘」作「月餘」，顯誤，今改正。

translations.literal: Multiply circuit-day day remainder by damage rate: all editions read "month remainder" for "day remainder"—clearly wrong; emended.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply circuit-day day remainder by damage rate: all editions read 月餘 for 日餘—clearly wrong; emended.

sentences.zh: 不盡為小分 諸本脫「為」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: What is not exhausted is the small part: all editions omit the character "is"; supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: What is not exhausted is the small part: all editions omit 為; supplied according to the sense of the text.

sentences.zh: 不盡為小分 諸本脫「分」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: What is not exhausted is the small part: all editions omit the character "part"; supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: What is not exhausted is the small part: all editions omit 分; supplied according to the sense of the text.

sentences.zh: 不滿宿者算外 諸本脫「外」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: What does not fill a lodge, count exclusive: all editions omit the character "exclusive"; supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: What does not fill a lodge, count exclusive: all editions omit 外; supplied according to the sense of the text.

sentences.zh: 次月合朔 諸本脫「次」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: Next-month new-moon conjunction: in 諸本 the character 次 is missing; it is now supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “next month’s new-moon conjunction”: all editions (諸本) omit the character 次; it is supplied herein on grounds of textual sense.

sentences.zh: 即次沒日 諸本「日」作「月」，今依文義改。

translations.literal: That is, the next extinction day: in 諸本 日 reads as 月; it is now emended according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “that is, the next extinction day”: in all editions (諸本) 日 appears as 月; the reading is emended herein according to textual sense.

sentences.zh: 沒餘滿蔀法從沒日 諸本脫「沒餘」及「法」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: When the extinction remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry from the extinction day: in 諸本 沒餘 and 法 are missing; they are now supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “when the extinction remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry from the extinction day”: all editions (諸本) omit 沒餘 and 法; both are supplied herein on grounds of textual sense.

sentences.zh: 曆月大小除之 諸本「月」作「日」，今依文義改。

translations.literal: Divide by the calendrical month’s great and small [portions]: in 諸本 月 reads as 日; it is now emended according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “divide by the calendrical month’s great and small portions”: in all editions (諸本) 月 appears as 日; the reading is emended herein according to textual sense.

sentences.zh: 小餘滿蔀法從大餘 諸本脫「法」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: When the minor remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry from the major remainder: in 諸本 法 is missing; it is now supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “when the minor remainder fills the obscuration divisor, carry from the major remainder”: all editions (諸本) omit 法; it is supplied herein on grounds of textual sense.

sentences.zh: 田鼠化為鴽 諸本脫「化」字。

translations.literal: Field mice transform into quails: in 諸本 the character 化 is missing.
translations.idiomatic: On “field mice transform into quails”: all editions (諸本) omit the character 化.

sentences.zh: 按禮月令：「田鼠化為鴽」，本志下興和曆推七十二候也作「田鼠化為鴽」。

translations.literal: Commentary: the Monthly Ordinances in the Rites reads “field mice transform into quails”; the treatise below, in the Xinghe calendar’s derivation of the seventy-two seasonal terms, likewise has “field mice transform into quails.”
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Monthly Ordinances in the Rites gives “field mice transform into quails,” and the Xinghe calendar’s derivation of the seventy-two seasonal terms later in this treatise uses the same wording.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The character is restored on that authority.

sentences.zh: 以六十去之 諸本「六十」作「六千」。

translations.literal: Remove it by sixty: in 諸本 六十 reads as 六千.
translations.idiomatic: On “remove it by sixty”: in all editions (諸本) 六十 appears as 六千.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「千字疑十字之訛。

translations.literal: 殿本考證 states: “The character 千 is suspected to be a corruption of 十.
translations.idiomatic: 殿本考證 observes: “The character 千 is likely a corruption of 十.

sentences.zh: 又下卷作『以六旬去之』。

translations.literal: Moreover, the lower fascicle reads ‘remove it by six ten-day weeks.’”
translations.idiomatic: The lower fascicle likewise reads, ‘remove it by six ten-day weeks.’”

sentences.zh: 」按考證說是，今據改。

translations.literal: ” Commentary: the verification’s explanation is correct; it is now emended on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: ” The verification is accepted; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑 諸本「熒惑」下有「星」字。

translations.literal: The essence of fire is called the Sparkling Deluder: below 熒惑 in 諸本 there is the character 星.
translations.idiomatic: On “the essence of fire is called the Sparkling Deluder”: all editions (諸本) add the character 星 after 熒惑.

sentences.zh: 按據各史五星命名及後興和曆例，熒惑下「星」字衍，今刪。

translations.literal: Commentary: judging from the naming of the five stars in the various histories and from the later Xinghe calendar’s precedents, the character 星 below 熒惑 is spurious; it is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: On the authority of the five-planet nomenclature in the various histories and the Xinghe calendar’s precedents, the character 星 after 熒惑 is redundant and is deleted.

sentences.zh: 其數二百二十九萬一千二十一 諸本「二百」作「三百」。

translations.literal: Its number is 2,291,021: in 諸本 二百 reads as 三百.
translations.idiomatic: On “its number is 2,291,021”: in all editions (諸本) 二百 appears as 三百.

sentences.zh: 按以鎮星合終日數三百七十八日乘蔀法六千六十，并以餘三百四十一，得二百二十九萬一千二十一。

translations.literal: Commentary: taking the Quelling Star’s total conjunction days, 378 days, multiplying by the obscuration divisor 6,060, and further using the remainder 341, one obtains 2,291,021.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation: the Quelling Star’s total conjunction of 378 days, multiplied by the obscuration divisor 6,060 and combined with the remainder 341, yields 2,291,021.

sentences.zh: 原文「三百」誤，今改正。

translations.literal: In the original text 三百 is erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original reading “three hundred” is in error and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 退十二度 諸本「十二」作「十三」。

translations.literal: Retreat twelve degrees: in 諸本 十二 reads as 十三.
translations.idiomatic: On “retreat twelve degrees”: in all editions (諸本) 十二 appears as 十三.

sentences.zh: 按日行七分之一，以七約八十四，得十二度。

translations.literal: Commentary: the daily motion is one-seventh of a degree; dividing 84 by 7 gives twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At one-seventh of a degree per day, 84 divided by 7 yields twelve degrees.

sentences.zh: 原文「三」誤，今改正。

translations.literal: In the original text 三 is erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original reading is in error—thirteen should be twelve—and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 餘四千七百八十 諸本「八」下脫「十」字。

translations.literal: Remainder 4,780: below 八 in 諸本 the character 十 is missing.
translations.idiomatic: On “remainder 4,780”: all editions (諸本) omit the character 十 after 八.

sentences.zh: 按歲星在日後伏十六日、餘二千三百九十，在日前伏十六日、餘二千三百九十，則在日前後共伏三十二日、餘四千七百八十。

translations.literal: Commentary: the Year Star, after the sun, is in occultation sixteen days with remainder 2,390; before the sun, in occultation sixteen days with remainder 2,390—thus before and after the sun it is in occultation altogether thirty-two days with remainder 4,780.
translations.idiomatic: The Year Star occults sixteen days with remainder 2,390 after the sun, and sixteen days with remainder 2,390 before the sun; together that is thirty-two days of occultation with remainder 4,780.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The missing character is restored on that authority.

sentences.zh: 合終日餘五千一百八 諸本「一百」作「一十」。

translations.literal: Total conjunction day-remainder 5,108: in 諸本 一百 reads as 一十.
translations.idiomatic: On “total conjunction day-remainder 5,108”: in all editions (諸本) 一百 appears as 一十.

sentences.zh: 按熒惑數四百七十二萬五千八百四十八約以蔀法，得合終日數七百七十九，合終日餘五千一百八。

translations.literal: Commentary: the Sparkling Deluder’s number 4,725,848, reduced by the obscuration divisor, yields total conjunction days 779 and total conjunction day-remainder 5,108.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the Sparkling Deluder’s figure of 4,725,848 by the obscuration divisor gives 779 total conjunction days and a day-remainder of 5,108.

sentences.zh: 原文「十」字誤，今改正。

translations.literal: In the original text the character 十 is erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original character 十 is in error and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 六十二日退十七度 諸本「十」下脫「七」字。

translations.literal: In sixty-two days retreat seventeen degrees: below 十 in 諸本 the character 七 is missing.
translations.idiomatic: On “in sixty-two days retreat seventeen degrees”: all editions (諸本) omit the character 七 after 十.

sentences.zh: 按日行六十二分之十七，則六十二日應行十七度。

translations.literal: Commentary: the daily motion is seventeen parts in sixty-two; therefore in sixty-two days it should advance seventeen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen sixty-second parts per day, sixty-two days should yield seventeen degrees of motion.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The missing character is restored on that authority.

sentences.zh: 餘三千六百三十一 諸本「三十」作「四十」。

translations.literal: Remainder 3,631: in 諸本 三十 reads as 四十.
translations.idiomatic: On “remainder 3,631”: in all editions (諸本) 三十 appears as 四十.

sentences.zh: 按熒惑在日後，伏，行星五十五度、餘四千八百四十五半；

translations.literal: Commentary: the Sparkling Deluder, after the sun, in occultation, stellar motion fifty-five degrees with remainder 4,845 and a half;
translations.idiomatic: After the sun the Sparkling Deluder occults with fifty-five degrees of stellar motion and remainder 4,845 and a half;

sentences.zh: 在日前，伏，行星五十五度、餘四千八百四十五半，則日前後伏時共行星一百一十一度、餘三千六百三十一。

translations.literal: before the sun, in occultation, stellar motion fifty-five degrees with remainder 4,845 and a half—thus at occultation before and after the sun it advances the star altogether one hundred eleven degrees with remainder 3,631.
translations.idiomatic: and before the sun it occults with fifty-five degrees of stellar motion and remainder 4,845 and a half; taken together, occultation before and after the sun yields one hundred eleven degrees of stellar motion with remainder 3,631.

sentences.zh: 原文「四十」誤，今改正。

translations.literal: In the original text 四十 is erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original reading “forty” is in error and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 日行十七分之一 諸本「行」上脫「日」字，今依文義補。

translations.literal: Daily motion one-seventeenth [of a degree]: above 行 in 諸本 the character 日 is missing; it is now supplied according to the sense of the text.
translations.idiomatic: On “daily motion one-seventeenth of a degree”: all editions (諸本) omit 日 before 行; it is supplied herein on grounds of textual sense.

sentences.zh: 行星二百四十四度 諸本「十」下脫「四」字。

translations.literal: Stellar motion two hundred forty-four degrees: below 十 in 諸本 the character 四 is missing.
translations.idiomatic: On “stellar motion two hundred forty-four degrees”: all editions (諸本) omit the character 四 after 十.

sentences.zh: 按依太白於東方所見各日行星度，順加、逆減，共計行星度當為二百四十四。

translations.literal: Commentary: according to the degrees of stellar motion on each day when the Great White is seen in the east, adding in direct motion and subtracting in retrograde motion, the total stellar motion should be two hundred forty-four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Summing the Great White’s daily degrees of motion when seen in the east—adding in direct motion and subtracting in retrograde—the total stellar motion should be two hundred forty-four degrees.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The missing character is restored on that authority.

sentences.zh: 在日後伏四十一日餘五千六百五半行星五十一度餘五千六百五半 按太白在日後先伏六日，退四度；

translations.literal: After the sun, in occultation forty-one days with remainder 5,605 and a half, stellar motion fifty-one degrees with degree-remainder 5,605 and a half. Commentary: the Great White, after the sun, first occults six days and retreats four degrees;
translations.idiomatic: “After the sun, occultation of forty-one days with remainder 5,605 and a half, and stellar motion of fifty-one degrees with degree-remainder 5,605 and a half.” Note: after the sun the Great White first occults six days and retreats four degrees;

sentences.zh: 次伏四十一日、餘五千六百五半，順，行星五十一度、度餘五千六百五半，共伏四十七日、餘五千六百五半，行星四十七度、度餘五千六百五半。

translations.literal: then occults forty-one days with remainder 5,605 and a half; in direct motion, stellar motion fifty-one degrees with degree-remainder 5,605 and a half—in all, occultation forty-seven days with remainder 5,605 and a half, stellar motion forty-seven degrees with degree-remainder 5,605 and a half.
translations.idiomatic: then occults forty-one days with remainder 5,605 and a half while advancing fifty-one degrees in direct motion with the same degree-remainder; in total that is forty-seven days of occultation with remainder 5,605 and a half and forty-seven degrees of stellar motion with the same degree-remainder.

sentences.zh: 「四十一日」當作「四十七日」，「五十一度」當作「四十七度」。

translations.literal: “Forty-one days” should read “forty-seven days”; “fifty-one degrees” should read “forty-seven degrees.”
translations.idiomatic: “Forty-one days” should read “forty-seven days,” and “fifty-one degrees” should read “forty-seven degrees.”

sentences.zh: 原文未將先伏之六日、退四度計算在內，以致錯誤；

translations.literal: The original text failed to include in the calculation the prior occultation of six days and retreat of four degrees, thereby causing error;
translations.idiomatic: The original text did not account for the initial six-day occultation and four-degree retreat, which led to the error;

sentences.zh: 下前後伏總計數亦同。

translations.literal: The totals for occultation before and after below are the same.
translations.idiomatic: the aggregate figures for occultation before and after the sun below are affected in the same way.

sentences.zh: 凡再見四百八十八日行星四百八十八度 諸本兩「八十」下俱脫「八」字。

translations.literal: In all, two appearances four hundred eighty-eight days, stellar motion four hundred eighty-eight degrees: in 諸本 under both instances of 八十 the character 八 is missing.
translations.idiomatic: On “in all, two appearances totaling four hundred eighty-eight days and four hundred eighty-eight degrees of stellar motion”: in all editions (諸本) both occurrences of 八十 lack the character 八.

sentences.zh: 按太白見東方二百四十四日，行星二百四十四度；

translations.literal: Commentary: the Great White, seen in the east two hundred forty-four days, stellar motion two hundred forty-four degrees;
translations.idiomatic: The Great White is seen in the east for two hundred forty-four days with two hundred forty-four degrees of stellar motion;

sentences.zh: 見西方亦二百四十四日，行星二百四十四度，凡再見共四百八十八日，行星四百八十八度。

translations.literal: seen in the west likewise two hundred forty-four days, stellar motion two hundred forty-four degrees—in all, two appearances together four hundred eighty-eight days, stellar motion four hundred eighty-eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: and in the west likewise for two hundred forty-four days with two hundred forty-four degrees; two appearances together thus yield four hundred eighty-eight days and four hundred eighty-eight degrees of motion.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The missing characters are restored on that authority.

sentences.zh: 在日前後伏八十三日餘五千一百五十一行星一百三度 按「八十三日」當作「九十五日」，「一百三度」當作「九十五度」，原文計算錯誤。

translations.literal: Before and after the sun, occultation eighty-three days with remainder 5,151, stellar motion one hundred three degrees. Commentary: “eighty-three days” should read “ninety-five days”; “one hundred three degrees” should read “ninety-five degrees”—the original text’s calculation is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: “Occultation before and after the sun of eighty-three days with remainder 5,151, and stellar motion of one hundred three degrees.” Note: “eighty-three days” should read “ninety-five days,” and “one hundred three degrees” should read “ninety-five degrees”; the original calculation is in error.

sentences.zh: 詳見校勘記[五一]。

translations.literal: See the Collation Note [五一] in detail.
translations.idiomatic: For full discussion see Collation Note [五一].

sentences.zh: 行星三十四度 諸本「三十」作「四十」。

translations.literal: Stellar motion thirty-four degrees: in 諸本 三十 reads as 四十.
translations.idiomatic: On “stellar motion thirty-four degrees”: in all editions (諸本) 三十 appears as 四十.

sentences.zh: 按下辰星在日前伏時行星度數作「三十四」，參照伏時總行星度，「四十四」乃「三十四」之誤，今改正。

translations.literal: Commentary: below, when the Chronogram Star is in occultation before the sun, the degrees of stellar motion are given as “thirty-four”; comparing with the total degrees of stellar motion during occultation, “forty-four” is an error for “thirty-four”; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Below, the Chronogram Star’s degrees of motion during occultation before the sun are given as thirty-four; measured against the total degrees during occultation, “forty-four” is a mistake for “thirty-four” and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 行星二十九度 諸本「九」作「二」。

translations.literal: Stellar motion twenty-nine degrees: in 諸本 九 reads as 二.
translations.idiomatic: On “stellar motion twenty-nine degrees”: in all editions (諸本) 九 appears as 二.

sentences.zh: 按辰星晨見東方，先行五度，次行二十四度，共行星二十九度。

translations.literal: Commentary: the Chronogram Star, seen in the morning in the east, first advances five degrees, then advances twenty-four degrees—in all, stellar motion twenty-nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chronogram Star appears in the morning east, it first advances five degrees and then twenty-four, for a total stellar motion of twenty-nine degrees.

sentences.zh: 原文顯誤，今改正。

translations.literal: The original text is clearly erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original reading is plainly in error and is corrected herein.

sentences.zh: 行星三十四度餘五千六百七十一 按辰星在日後，先伏十一日，退六度；

translations.literal: Stellar motion thirty-four degrees with remainder 5,671. Commentary: the Chronogram Star, after the sun, first occults eleven days and retreats six degrees;
translations.idiomatic: “Stellar motion of thirty-four degrees with remainder 5,671.” Note: after the sun the Chronogram Star first occults eleven days and retreats six degrees;

sentences.zh: 次伏十七日、餘五千六百七十一，順，行星三十四度、餘五千六百七十一，共伏二十八日、餘五千六百七十一，行星二十八度、餘五千六百七十一。

translations.literal: then occults seventeen days with remainder 5,671; in direct motion, stellar motion thirty-four degrees with remainder 5,671—in all, occultation twenty-eight days with remainder 5,671, stellar motion twenty-eight degrees with remainder 5,671.
translations.idiomatic: then occults seventeen days with remainder 5,671 while advancing thirty-four degrees in direct motion with the same remainder; in total that is twenty-eight days of occultation with remainder 5,671 and twenty-eight degrees of stellar motion with the same remainder.

sentences.zh: 志未將先伏退行度數減去，致總日數未誤，而總行星度數「二十八」誤作「三十四」；

translations.literal: The treatise failed to subtract the degrees of the prior occultation’s retrograde motion, so that the total days were not wrong, but the total degrees of stellar motion had “twenty-eight” wrongly written as “thirty-four”;
translations.idiomatic: The treatise did not subtract the retrograde degrees from the initial occultation; the total days are unaffected, but the aggregate stellar motion wrongly reads thirty-four instead of twenty-eight;

sentences.zh: 下前后伏總行星度數亦同以致誤。

translations.literal: The totals for stellar motion before and after occultation below are likewise affected, causing error.
translations.idiomatic: the combined stellar-motion totals for occultation before and after the sun below are wrong for the same reason.

sentences.zh: 行星四十六度 按辰星見東方，共行星二十九度，見西方，亦行星二十九度，再見共行星五十八度。

translations.literal: Stellar motion forty-six degrees. Commentary: the Chronogram Star, seen in the east, stellar motion altogether twenty-nine degrees; seen in the west, likewise stellar motion twenty-nine degrees—two appearances together stellar motion fifty-eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: “Stellar motion forty-six degrees.” Note: the Chronogram Star moves twenty-nine degrees when seen in the east and twenty-nine when seen in the west; two appearances together yield fifty-eight degrees.

sentences.zh: 志誤。

translations.literal: The treatise is in error.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 行星六十九度 按「六十九」當作「五十七」，詳見校勘記[五六]。

translations.literal: Stellar motion sixty-nine degrees. Commentary: “sixty-nine” should read “fifty-seven”; see Collation Note [五六] in detail.
translations.idiomatic: “Stellar motion sixty-nine degrees.” Note: “sixty-nine” should read “fifty-seven”; for full discussion see Collation Note [五六].
